articles.title: County Championship cricket: Ben Stokes helps Durham to victory as title-chasing Nottinghamshire draw with Leicestershire
articles.summary: Former England Test captain Ben Stokes takes revenge on Northamptonshire's Yuzvendra Chahal in Durham's victory; Nottinghamshire suffer double frustration as they draw with Leicestershire and lose wicketkeeper Kyle Verreynne for rest of County Championship season
articles.body:
After Durham got up to 261 in their second innings to set Northants a victory target of 204 at the start of day four, Callum Parkinson raced through the hosts' batting line-up in stunning fashion on his way to 6-20.

Stokes then finished the job when he had the last laugh on Yuzvendra Chahal, who had dismissed the former England captain with a wonder delivery in the first innings, but was caught behind for 10 with Northamptonshire dismissed for only 50.

Elsewhere in the second tier, Kent were able to make the most of Northamptonshire's defeat to boost their own promotion hopes with victory by an 84-run margin at home to Worcestershire.

After the away side resumed day four on 84-3 with a victory target of 380, they were all out for 295 despite an unbeaten 103 by captain Brett D'Oliveira with Matt Milnes, Hasan Mahmud and Keith Dudgeon taking three wickets each for Kent.

Kent now boast a 15-point advantage over third-placed Northants in the battle to go up to Division One.

Elsewhere, Gloucestershire secured a remarkable victory by 213 runs against Derbyshire after the visitors collapsed to 105 all out.

Sai Kishore picked up five wickets after James Bracey's 104 not out had helped the hosts declare on 359-5.

Notts title hopes hit after draw at Leicestershire

In Division One, Nottinghamshire had to settle for a draw at Leicestershire , who resumed on 250-7 and made it up to 358 before Haseeb Hameed struck a century for the home team in the second innings at Trent Bridge.

The result leaves Notts four points behind Somerset in the race for the title with three rounds of matches still to play.

Their hopes took a further blow when it was announced that Kyle Verreynne will miss the rest of the season after being recalled home early by Cricket South Africa.

Wicketkeeper Verreynne had originally signed to play all of Nottinghamshire's Championship matches this summer, but he has been recalled early along with several other South Africans playing in England.

Nottinghamshire Director of Cricket, Mick Newell, said: "It's not ideal that we're losing Kyle at this point in the season, but we understand the decision."

Matt Critchley fell four runs short of a century and could not prevent Essex from losing by 47 runs to Sussex in pursuit of 329. James Coles was the pick of the bowlers for the visitors with 4-98 at Chelmsford.

articles.title: 4 bold predictions for the Chargers' defense in 2026
articles.summary: From defensive takeaways to star-studded performances, these four bold predictions showcase how we expect the Chargers' defense to perform in 2026.
articles.body:
The Chargers have a ton going for them as the 2026 season approaches, and much of that has to do with their defense.

Los Angeles has a chance to continue to be one of the league's best defenses under Chris O'Leary, just as they were with Jesse Minter calling the shots over the last two seasons.

The Chargers' defense has a lot on the line, and it's time to put some bold predictions on the table.

4. Daiyan Henley finishes as the Chargers' leading tackler, named Pro Bowler

We're coming in hot with the first one. The first part of that prediction is far from bold, as Henley led the team in tackles last season with 103. The second part is certainly the definition of bold. He's already shown flashes of playing at a Pro Bowl-caliber level. However, in 2026, Henley is expected to step into a definitive leadership role and be the anchor of the middle for the Chargers' defense. If Henley can have it all come together on a week-to-week basis, Henley has a great chance to earn that nod.

3. Genesis Smith quickly emerges as a pillar of the Chargers' secondary

We have to show the rookie some love. Smith, the fourth-round pick, doesn't have to become a superstar overnight for this prediction to hit. Nonetheless, he possesses elite centerfield range, high-upside ball-hawking instincts, and a modern defensive scheme that maximizes his strengths. Smith will have to continue improving in the tackling department, but the coverage skills should allow him to flourish very quickly.

2. The Chargers finish with a top-five scoring defense

The Chargers finished ninth in this area, and with what I believe is an improved unit, personnel-wise, this is well within reach. Los Angeles has enough talent to make a significant jump defensively, and the biggest reason to believe it is the number of playmakers they have at every level. If health is on their side and the young guys develop quickly, the Bolts could go from simply a good defense to one of the NFL's most difficult units to score against.

1. Akheem Mesidor leads the team in sacks

The rookie edge rusher has shown that he can come into the league and make an immediate impact on the Chargers' defense. Mesidor doesn't have the best player on the defensive line, but he does need to take advantage of the opportunities that come with playing alongside established players like Khalil Mack and Tuli Tuipulotu. With Mack and Tuipulotu there, Mesidor could likely benefit from more favorable one-on-one matchups. If he can take advantage of that, there's a realistic path to him leading the team in sacks. In his final college season, Mesidor had 12.5 sacks.

articles.title: ‘Even my wife is watching’: Srikkanth says Vaibhav Sooryavanshi is making cricket exciting again
articles.summary: Cricket News: NEW DELHI: Former India opener Kris Srikkanth believes Vaibhav Sooryavanshi has the potential to become one of the biggest names in world cricket, wit.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Former India opener Kris Srikkanth believes Vaibhav Sooryavanshi has the potential to become one of the biggest names in world cricket, with the teenage sensation already generating an unusual level of excitement around the game.Sooryavanshi, just 15, has continued his rapid rise by making a mark in the Duleep Trophy after already setting the IPL and international stages alight. For Srikkanth, however, the youngster's impact is going beyond numbers — he is making people tune in to cricket they might otherwise have overlooked.“He's playing outstandingly well. He must be encouraged and never be discouraged. If he's moulded properly, he'll be a superstar in the making. He'll bring Test cricket back to its glory. Everyone watched the Duleep Trophy because of him. Even my wife is watching because of him. He'll be a big asset going forward for World cricket,” Srikkanth said on his YouTube channel.‘He’ll be a superstar in the making’Sooryavanshi has certainly given fans plenty to watch. After failing to make an impact in East Zone's quarterfinal win over North East Zone, he responded emphatically against Central Zone in the semifinal.The teenager smashed 92 off 81 balls in the first innings and then contributed a crucial 40 in the final innings as East Zone secured a four-wicket victory to book their place in the final.At 15 years and 157 days, Sooryavanshi had already become the youngest batter to score a half-century in Duleep Trophy history, breaking a 57-year-old record.Srikkanth was particularly impressed by the teenager's fearless approach in red-ball cricket and believes there is little reason to question his ability to make the jump to the highest level.“He played incredibly well. How can people even doubt whether this boy on whether he is capable of playing higher-level cricket? He can play every level of cricket, and he is going to rule world cricket shortly in all formats. He's smashing medium pacers with no worries for straight sixes in red-ball cricket. He's toying with the bowlers,” he said.From IPL sensation to India starSooryavanshi's rise has been extraordinary. His breakthrough IPL 2026 campaign with Rajasthan Royals saw him score 776 runs in 16 matches at a staggering strike rate of 237.30, including a century and five fifties. His 72 sixes were an IPL record for a single season, while he collected the Orange Cap, Most Valuable Player, Emerging Player, Super Striker and Super Sixes awards.He subsequently became India's youngest men's international debutant during the T20I series against England. Against Zimbabwe, he scored 151 runs in three matches to help India complete a 3-0 sweep and collected his maiden Player of the Series award.His impact has also extended to age-group cricket. Earlier this year, Sooryavanshi amassed 439 runs at the ICC Under-19 World Cup and was named Player of the Tournament.The BCCI is now taking a cautious, long-term approach to his development. Secretary Devajit Saikia said the board is monitoring the teenager closely and wants his early success to translate into a career similar to those of India's past legends.“We want Vaibhav Sooryavanshi or any player of his stature to continue and serve like Sachin Tendulkar did for the country or other players who in the past became legends,” Saikia said.“So we look at Vaibhav in a very serious manner. He's monitored from every angle and every step he is taking forward in his international career. The BCCI is taking a very close look at his future.”The board's priority, Saikia stressed, is to ensure Sooryavanshi's emergence is not merely a brief burst of teenage brilliance.“You see, the BCCI can be proud that we are promoting a player of the age of 15 years who is already making his mark in the international scenario and we are very cautious that every right step he should take forward so that it should not be a one series or one year wonder,” he said.For now, though, Srikkanth sees something even bigger taking shape — a youngster whose fearless cricket is making people sit up and watch.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: No special ‘room’ for cricket: IOA draws line on BCCI’s Asian Games stay
articles.summary: Cricket News: New Delhi: If the BCCI decides its cricketers need to stay outside the official Asian Games hotels in Aichi-Nagoya, the board will have to take full r.
articles.body: New Delhi: If the BCCI decides its cricketers need to stay outside the official Asian Games hotels in Aichi-Nagoya, the board will have to take full responsibility for accommodation, food, transport and ensuring that its players reach the venue on time. The Indian Olympic Association (IOA), meanwhile, will not seek separate accommodation arrangements for cricket, as it’s for the cricket body and Organising Committee (OC) to work out an amicable solution.IOA CEO Raghuram Iyer, speaking to TOI, said the BCCI is free to make its own arrangements if the organisers’ hotels don’t suit its requirements, but the decision and the accompanying logistical responsibility would rest with the Board. The IOA, he stressed, has to ensure equal treatment and the welfare of the entire Indian contingent across 36 sports.“BCCI CEO Hemang Amin got in touch with us (IOA), and we had a fruitful discussion. They are contemplating sending an advance team to Japan to assess the facilities. The IOA is completely fine with that. Based on their assessment, they can decide whether they want to use the organisers’ facilities or make their own arrangements. It is for the BCCI and the organisers to work out the best solution. All sports, athletes, coaches and the entire delegation are treated equally by IOA,” Iyer said.For now, the Games organisers have a designated accommodation plan for both Indian teams. The men have been allotted the three-star APA Hotel Nagoya Ekimae, while the women have been assigned the four-star Meitetsu Grand Hotel, it’s been learnt. Both properties possess the requisite amenities, though they are a grade below the five-star accommodation to which India’s cricketers are generally accustomed. Rooms will be on a twin-sharing basis, another major bone of contention.The women, captained by Harmanpreet Kaur, face the first logistical test. They return from the Asia Cup in Dubai on Sept 13 and are scheduled to fly to Nagoya the following day. Their Asian Games campaign begins directly in the quarterfinals on Sept 18, with their tournament scheduled to conclude on Sept 22.The men, led by Shreyas Iyer, will travel later, leaving for Japan on Sept 21. They too enter directly at the quarterfinal stage, with their campaign running from Sept 28 and the team scheduled to return on Oct 4.With both teams having different arrival windows, the BCCI is now looking at the accommodation and logistics from its own perspective. An advance team is travelling to Japan early next week to inspect the hotels, cricket venue and other facilities before the Board takes a final call, sources revealed.The availability of suitable alternatives could be crucial. Aichi-Nagoya is already under considerable accommodation pressure, with the number of athletes and coaches expected to rise to around 17,000 from an original planning figure of 15,000. Existing hotels are being supplemented by mobile accommodation and the Costa Serena cruise ship.If the BCCI decides the official hotels do not work for its teams and opts for separate properties, it will have to arrange the entire operation, including rooms, food, local transport and travel to and from the cricket venue, while ensuring the players reach the ground well ahead of match time.That arrangement, however, would not put the cricketers outside the Games system. The BCCI would have to communicate its decision through the IOA to the organisers, and all Games-related security, accreditation and access protocols would continue to apply. Outsiders without valid accreditation would not be permitted into the team hotels.The separate stay would also have implications for anti-doping procedures. WADA and International Testing Agency (ITA) dope-control officers would have to be informed of the players’ location so that random testing can be carried out at their chosen accommodation.Iyer said the IOA was comfortable with the BCCI assessing what works best for its players.“The BCCI is taking care of its athletes, and sending an advance team is the right way to assess the facilities before making a decision. We are completely for the well-being of the athletes. Our objective is that the entire Indian delegation has a comfortable stay and a wonderful experience in Japan,” he said.The contrast with Los Angeles 2028 is already emergingWhile Japan’s cricket arrangements have prompted scrutiny, planning for cricket’s Olympic return at Los Angeles 2028 is already well advanced. Iyer was part of a joint IOA-Sports Authority of India (SAI) delegation that recently spent nearly a week in Los Angeles, meeting stakeholders and inspecting facilities across sports, including cricket.“The objective is to ensure athletes can focus only on their performance and do not face logistical issues. We are thinking well in advance about their welfare, comfort and acclimatisation, and this is something which is happening for the first time,” Iyer said.Cricket’s LA28 venue, the newly built Knight Riders Cricket Ground at the Fairplex complex in Pomona, is located next to the Sheraton Fairplex Suites & Conference Center, where the cricket teams are expected to be accommodated. Major League Cricket matches are also expected to provide an early competitive test of the new venue and playing surface.Before the Asian Games, India and Japan will also share a historic cricketing moment. Their men’s teams meet in a T20I on Sept 22 for the Suzuki Cup, marking 75 years of diplomatic relations and giving India valuable match practice ahead of the Games.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: ‘Don’t call it cricket’: Ricky Ponting makes radical T20 pitch to win over US fans
articles.summary: Cricket News: Australian great Ricky Ponting has suggested a radical change in the way cricket is marketed in the United States, saying administrators should consid.
articles.body: Australian great Ricky Ponting has suggested a radical change in the way cricket is marketed in the United States, saying administrators should consider dropping the word ‘cricket’ altogether and promoting the sport simply as ‘T20’.With the United States emerging as a key part of the International Cricket Council (ICC)’s global growth strategy, Ponting believes the traditional name could be holding the sport back in a market more familiar with baseball, American football and basketball.The former Australia captain feels the word ‘cricket’ could lead new American audiences to immediately think of Test matches and their five-day format, rather than the shorter and more entertainment-driven T20 game.Speaking to The Athletic, Ponting acknowledged that he is a traditionalist who played far more Test cricket than T20 cricket. However, he said he would be open to a complete rebranding of the format if it helped attract a new generation of American sports fans.“If I was bringing it here wholly and solely to sell and promote the game, I wouldn’t call it cricket," Ponting begins. “It’d just be rebranded as T20 only. Leave the cricket thing aside. As soon as young people hear cricket in parts of the world where they’re not brought up on the game, they think about it being a long, drawn-out, five-day game, and it’s not that."Ponting also believes baseball could provide a useful comparison for introducing T20 to an American audience. Rather than focusing on the technical differences between the sports, he wants potential fans to understand the high-scoring nature of the shortest cricket format.“I would compare it to baseball as much as I could and give kids that chance to understand you’re hitting 15 sixes per game in a game of T20 cricket, but you are hitting less than one home run a game in the game of baseball."The United States has become one of the ICC’s biggest development priorities, given the size and commercial strength of its sports market. While baseball, American football and basketball remain dominant, soccer has also been growing rapidly in the country.Cricket, meanwhile, has traditionally had a much smaller mainstream following in the US and has largely been played and followed by Asian, European and African expat communities.The ICC has been attempting to broaden that audience through a series of major initiatives. The country hosted a successful T20 World Cup in 2024, while Major League Cricket has been developed as a domestic competition. Ponting himself is involved in the league as coach of Washington Freedom.The ICC is also working towards cricket’s return to the Olympic stage at the Los Angeles 2028 Games, with efforts underway to develop suitable grounds and infrastructure in the US.With T20 at the centre of many of those efforts, Ponting believes presenting the sport as a fast-paced, modern product rather than immediately associating it with Test cricket could help the ICC connect with American audiences.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Pakiatan coach explodes over King Charles report: 'Someone's just made something up'
articles.summary: Cricket News: Pakistan's interim Test coach Mike Hesson has denied reports that Salman Ali Agha refused to attend a meeting with King Charles III, saying the story .
articles.body: Pakistan's interim Test coach Mike Hesson has denied reports that Salman Ali Agha refused to attend a meeting with King Charles III, saying the story was completely false and describing it as "unacceptable journalism."A report by UK-based The Telegraph on Thursday claimed that one of the players dropped from Pakistan's Test squad had refused to attend a meeting with the UK monarch.Hesson dismissed the report and said Salman had been informed well in advance that he would not be part of the Buckingham Palace visit.Hesson said Salman did not attend the audience with the King because he was part of the trio of players dropped from the squad first and, as a result, Salman, Imam and Rizwan were taken from the list of attendees to Clarence House, BBC reported."Look, I know there's been a void in the news, but people are just making up stories. Salman Ali Agha, as I've said, the three players were released from the squad before I arrived, well before Buckingham Palace," Hesson said on Friday."They were sent a note at that time that these three players would not be attending Buckingham Palace. So, someone's just made something up," he added.Hesson said the players who remained with the squad had already been invited to the event and there were no last-minute changes."In terms of the other players, all of the rest of the players that were in the squad were already on the list. I was already on the list as the white-ball head coach, so there have been no changes to it," he said."It was all very straightforward. Someone's just got two and two together and come up with nine. For me, that's unacceptable journalism," Hesson added.Pakistan's coaching and squad changes came after defeats in the first two Tests against England.Pakistan lost the first Test at Headingley by an innings and 103 runs before suffering a 194-run defeat at Lord's, giving England an unassailable 2-0 lead in the three-match series.The Pakistan Cricket Board then made drastic changes, sending seven players home, calling up another seven players and replacing Test head coach Sarfaraz Ahmed with Hesson, who was already serving as Pakistan's white-ball head coach.Senior players Imam-ul-Haq and Salman Ali Agha, who captained Pakistan in the first Test at Headingley when Babar Azam was injured, were among the players asked to leave the tour.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. We are monitoring him from every angle and every step he takes in his international career,” Saikia said.Sooryavanshi has rapidly progressed from IPL sensation to India’s youngest men’s international debutant. He recently became the youngest player to score a Duleep Trophy fifty, hammering 92 off 81 balls, including seven sixes, for East Zone against Central Zone in Bengaluru.Making it clear that the BCCI is focused on longevity rather than instant success, Saikia added: “We are very cautious that every step he takes forward is the right one so that he does not become a one-series or one-year wonder.”Like Tendulkar, Sooryavanshi has burst onto the international scene as a teenager and quickly captured the imagination of Indian cricket fans. The left-hander earned his maiden India call-up after two sensational seasons with Rajasthan Royals.In IPL 2026, he piled up 776 runs in 16 matches at a staggering strike rate of 237.30, scoring a century and five fifties while smashing a record 72 sixes in a single season. After a slow start in England, he bounced back impressively in the T20I series against Zimbabwe, scoring 151 runs in three matches and claiming his first Player of the Series award.Asiad facilities not a concernMeanwhile, Saikia said the BCCI has no immediate concerns about accommodation or facilities for India’s cricket teams at the Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya.“There is no such issue which we have discussed or which is in our agenda,” he said.However, he made it clear that the board would step in if required.“If any situation arises, we will ensure our players and support staff get the best facilities. articles.title: ‘Behavioural issues’ behind Mohammed Rizwan, Imam-ul-Haq axe? Fresh details emerge from PCB shock move
articles.summary: Cricket News: The Pakistan Cricket Board’s decision to send seven players and two coaches home after defeats in the first two Tests against England continues to thr.
articles.body: The Pakistan Cricket Board’s decision to send seven players and two coaches home after defeats in the first two Tests against England continues to throw up fresh details, with behavioural concerns reportedly playing a role in the removal of senior players Mohammad Rizwan, Imam-ul-Haq and Salman Ali Agha.Pakistan suffered defeats in the opening two matches of the series, prompting the PCB to make a sweeping change ahead of the third and final Test in Edgbaston. Test coach Sarfaraz has already been replaced by Mike Hesson, while the white-ball coach will oversee the team for the final Test.Rizwan’s performances were one of the concerns surrounding the wicketkeeper-batter. He managed just 61 runs across the four innings he played and came under further criticism for his shot selection during the Lord’s Test. His reading of the game also attracted scrutiny.Imam, meanwhile, did not bat in either innings at Lord’s after suffering a calf strain. His decision not to take the field with the bat sparked questions over his commitment, with his injury becoming a major talking point.Agha’s situation was different. He captained Pakistan in the first Test in Babar’s absence but was dropped for the second match before being sent home ahead of the Edgbaston Test.According to news agency PTI, however, the decisions involving Rizwan and Imam were not linked exclusively to their performances. Behavioural issues in the dressing room were also reportedly taken into consideration.The trio of Rizwan, Imam and Agha are now expected to appear before a committee and explain their conduct in connection with certain incidents during Pakistan’s tours of the West Indies and England.The other players sent back from England were reportedly removed from the squad following Hesson’s recommendation. The interim red-ball head coach wanted to assess several white-ball specialists with whom he had previously worked.“The rest of the players sent back were done so on the recommendation of interim red-ball head coach Mike Hesson, who wanted to try out some players he had worked with in the white-ball camp,” a source said.Aaqib Javed under pressureThe latest developments are also expected to have consequences for Pakistan’s selection committee. Senior selector Aaqib Javed could be removed as part of a wider clean-up being planned by PCB chairman Mohsin Naqvi.Another major development came earlier this week when selector Misbah-ul-Haq tendered his resignation. It remains unclear whether the PCB has formally accepted it.Misbah’s resignation followed the PCB issuing a show-cause notice to the selection committee. The board sought an explanation over the inclusion of Imam and Rizwan in the Test squad for the West Indies and England tours.The PCB has also issued notices to members of its selection and advisory committees, asking them to explain the decision to pick Imam and Rizwan for the England tour and the criteria used to formulate the selection policy.The shake-up could lead to a new selection committee being appointed once the England tour concludes.“A new selection committee could be announced after the England tour,” the source said.Meanwhile, Hesson could remain in charge beyond the England series. articles.title: ‘CSK captaincy must be changed’: Sanju Samson backed to take over from Ruturaj Gaikwad
articles.summary: Cricket News: Chennai Super Kings have built their reputation on stability, but the franchise could be forced to make some major calls ahead of the 2027 Indian Prem.
articles.body: Chennai Super Kings have built their reputation on stability, but the franchise could be forced to make some major calls ahead of the 2027 Indian Premier League season.The five-time champions have endured a difficult phase, missing out on the playoffs for three successive seasons. Their 2026 campaign was further complicated by skipper Ruturaj Gaikwad’s struggles with the bat, while the arrival of Sanju Samson from Rajasthan Royals sparked debate over whether CSK could consider a leadership change.Although CSK have traditionally avoided knee-jerk decisions, former India batter Sadagoppan Ramesh has now backed Samson to take over the captaincy if the franchise decides to move on from Gaikwad.Samson brings considerable leadership experience from his time at Rajasthan Royals. The wicketkeeper-batter, who was named Player of the Tournament at the 2026 T20 World Cup, moved to CSK ahead of the 2026 IPL and finished the season as the franchise’s highest run-scorer.Ramesh believes those credentials make Samson a serious option for CSK."CSK are seemingly considering many options for the captaincy and even wondering whether a change is needed. Sanju Samson should be considered as captain because he’s such a fantastic team player. The CSK captaincy must be changed, and if it is, CSK must seriously consider Sanju Samson,” said Ramesh on his Instagram handle.He also pointed to Samson’s IPL captaincy record, while stressing that changing the skipper alone would not solve all of CSK’s problems.“Samson has also captained 66 matches in the IPL and won 33. So he has a 50% success rate. Under him, RR performed well, reaching the final and making another playoff appearance. Of course, CSK need several other things to change, and just making Sanju the captain won’t win them the trophy. But if at all they change captains, Sanju must be strongly considered,” he added.Gaikwad’s difficult 2026 seasonGaikwad’s position has come under scrutiny following a disappointing campaign in 2026.The right-hander scored 337 runs at an average of 28.08 and also recorded the lowest strike rate among all batters during the powerplay. His struggles added to the questions surrounding CSK’s leadership ahead of the next season.Ramesh is not the first former CSK player to suggest that Gaikwad could benefit from stepping away from the captaincy.Former CSK and India batter Subramaniam Badrinath had previously argued that Gaikwad should be relieved of leadership duties and allowed to concentrate entirely on his batting.“So once you remove him from captaincy, he’ll perform well as a batter. It won’t be a harsh decision if he is stripped of captaincy. It’s more beneficial for the player and the franchise. It’ll only do Gaikwad a world of good. This is not new to him alone. Even greats like Sachin Tendulkar have been affected by captaincy. If you are someone who is intense and thinks too much, it’s hard to detach from captaincy even while batting,” he had said on his YouTube channel.CSK themselves have several decisions to make before the 2027 season. The franchise are currently looking for a new head coach after Stephen Fleming stepped down earlier this year.There is also uncertainty surrounding MS Dhoni’s future, with it still unclear whether the former India captain will continue playing for CSK in the 2027 IPL.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: ‘Nothing left for the bowlers’: Suresh Raina sounds alarm over IPL impact player rule
articles.summary: Cricket News: Suresh Raina has become the latest former India cricketer to raise concerns over the impact player rule in the Indian Premier League (IPL), arguing th.
articles.body: Suresh Raina has become the latest former India cricketer to raise concerns over the impact player rule in the Indian Premier League (IPL), arguing that the experiment has significantly tilted the balance of the game towards batters.The former Chennai Super Kings (CSK) batter, who was part of four IPL-winning campaigns, believes bowlers have been particularly disadvantaged since the rule was introduced in 2023. The issue has remained a talking point among players, with Virat Kohli and Rohit Sharma also expressing their reservations about the rule during the 2024 season.Raina says impact player rule has made life difficult for bowlersThe impact player rule allows teams to name five substitute options after the toss, from which they can bring in one replacement at any point during the match. The teams first announce their batting and bowling XIs at the toss, while the designated replacement can be introduced after the first ball has been bowled.Raina believes the additional substitution option has played a major role in the explosion of batting in the IPL. Scores that once appeared difficult to chase have increasingly become achievable, with teams regularly crossing the 200-run mark and several 250-plus totals being recorded over the last three seasons.The trend was particularly evident during the 2024 edition, when Punjab Kings successfully chased down a target of more than 260 against Kolkata Knight Riders.Raina feels the growing emphasis on batting depth has left bowlers with fewer opportunities to influence matches.“I am against the Impact player rule. A lot of fit players also bat and just sit down. How will you improve? There is no such rule in the World Cup. I understand the entertainment factor, but there is nothing left for the bowlers. Earlier, 170 was a competitive score, but now 250 is being chased as well. Even 300 is being scored," Raina told the former India batter, Aakash Chopra.The former India international believes the rule has also reduced the consequences of losing wickets, as teams can bring in another specialist batter when required."Leave something for the bowlers. There is no wicket-taking option. The batters don't get out, and with extra batters, there will be pressure on the bowlers,” he added.Raina changes stance on Indian players in overseas leaguesRaina also addressed another long-standing debate surrounding Indian cricketers: whether they should be permitted to participate in overseas T20 leagues.The former India batter, who was part of India's 2011 World Cup-winning team, said he no longer believes there is a need for Indian players to feature in competitions such as Australia's Big Bash League (BBL) and England's Hundred.Raina revealed that he had previously been keen on playing in overseas leagues and had even come close to doing so. However, permission was not granted at the time.“I feel Indian players should not be allowed now. Our league has become very big. When we used to go on Australia and England tours before, I used to ask this. I had come close to playing as well, but then they said no," said Raina.'We are ruling the world': Raina backs IPL's standingAccording to Raina, the situation has changed considerably since those days. The IPL has grown into one of the biggest competitions in world cricket, while overseas leagues have increasingly relied on international players travelling to India for the tournament.He also feels the overall quality of some foreign T20 leagues has declined compared to the past, making it even less important for Indian players to gain experience abroad."Now, a lot of outside players come here, and the quality of foreign leagues has also gone down. Back then, I would have definitely said yes. But at this time, we are ruling the world. Cricket is going somewhere else, and our team is very solid,” he added.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: ‘Babar Azam the next target?’: Ex-Pakistan captain launches scathing attack on PCB over England Test chaos
articles.summary: Cricket News: The Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) is facing renewed criticism over its handling of the senior men's national team, with former captain Rashid Latif acc.
articles.body: The Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) is facing renewed criticism over its handling of the senior men's national team, with former captain Rashid Latif accusing the board of effectively running the side through “remote control” and questioning why coaches and captains are not being given greater authority.The latest criticism comes after the PCB made an unprecedented mid-series overhaul, sending seven players and two coaches back to Pakistan following defeats in the first two Tests against England.The sweeping changes have added to the uncertainty surrounding Pakistan's Test set-up, with several former players and prominent voices in the game questioning the timing and scale of the PCB's decision.Rashid Latif questions PCB's handling of coachesPakistan had already been under considerable pressure after losing the opening two Tests against England. However, rather than retaining the same group for the remainder of the series, the PCB opted for a major reshuffle.Among those sent home were senior players Mohammad Rizwan and Salman Ali Agha. Test coach Sarfaraz Ahmed was also removed from the set-up, with white-ball coach Mike Hesson taking charge for the third and final Test in Birmingham.Latif has now questioned why Sarfaraz and bowling coach Umar Gul were sent to the UK in the first place if the PCB intended to exercise such a high degree of control over the team.Taking to X, the former Pakistan captain also referred to the departures of Jason Gillespie and Gary Kirsten, both of whom previously stepped down after disagreements over the level of authority and freedom available to them.Latif also brought captain Babar Azam into the discussion, suggesting that if the captain was not following the team's preferred direction, the PCB should have removed him rather than sending coaches back home."If the team had to be run by remote control, then why were Sarfaraz and Umar Gul sent? Why were the selection powers taken away from Gary Kirsten and Jason Gillespie? And if captain Babar Azam wasn’t listening, the captain should have been sacked — so why were Sarfaraz and Umar Gul sent back instead? Is Babar Azam the next target?” Latif wrote on X.PCB faces backlash over seven-player overhaulThe PCB's decision to make such sweeping changes in the middle of a Test series has attracted criticism from several high-profile figures in Pakistan cricket.Michael Atherton, Nasser Hussain, Ramiz Raja, Basit Ali and Shahid Afridi have all questioned the move, with the critics arguing that such drastic changes could create even more instability within an already struggling Pakistan side.The PCB, however, has defended its decision.Chairman Mohsin Naqvi previously backed the overhaul, insisting that the board had taken the harsh step because it believed it was necessary for the betterment of the team.Pakistan's Test struggles continueThe dramatic changes come against the backdrop of Pakistan's prolonged struggles in the longest format.Pakistan are currently at the bottom of the World Test Championship (WTC) standings and have never been genuine contenders for a place in the WTC final during the current cycle.The latest campaign will also mark the fourth consecutive WTC cycle in which Pakistan finish in the bottom half of the standings, highlighting the extent of their problems in Test cricket.The defeat in England has only intensified the scrutiny surrounding the team's direction and the PCB's decision-making process.Another captaincy change under scrutinyPakistan's Test leadership has also undergone another change this year.Earlier in 2026, the PCB replaced Shan Masood with Babar Azam as Test captain after Bangladesh completed a 2-0 series victory over Pakistan.Babar's return to the leadership role initially brought some stability, with Pakistan drawing their two-Test series against the West Indies.However, the team's fortunes quickly deteriorated once the side arrived in England. After losing the opening two Tests, the PCB responded with a drastic squad overhaul, sending seven players and two members of the coaching staff home.That decision has now prompted fresh questions over who is actually making the key decisions within Pakistan cricket, with Latif's comments adding another layer to the growing controversy surrounding the board's handling of the national team.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'Those two little pals of mine': Sonny Ramadhin became first Indian-origin cricketer to play for West Indies in 1950, helped them beat England in England for the first time. He became part of first great West Indies team and a protagonist of one of cricket's most iconic songs
articles.summary: Cricket News: Sonny Ramadhin became the first cricketer of Indian origin to represent the West Indies when he made his Test debut at Old Trafford during the 1950 to.
articles.body: Sonny Ramadhin became the first cricketer of Indian origin to represent the West Indies when he made his Test debut at Old Trafford during the 1950 tour of England.Born in St Charles Village in Trinidad, not far from the capital Port of Spain, Ramadhin lost both his parents when he was a toddler. He was raised by his grandparents, who had migrated from India to work on one of Trinidad's cocoa estates.Ramadhin did not have a first name when he was born. He was simply called "boy" during his childhood. Over time, that became "Sonny", and the name stayed with him.Then something unusual happened during the 1950 tour of England. In Ramadhin's own words: "When I got to England they insisted that nobody could go through life without initials. The next time I picked up the paper I'd become KT Ramadhin. I never did find out what my new English names were supposed to be!"No matter what the English newspapers called him, he remained Sonny Ramadhin — the mystery spinner from the Caribbean who made the cricket world take notice in 1950.The spin twins Ramadhin and fellow spinner Alf Valentine became one of the biggest reasons behind West Indies' famous 3-1 Test series win over England in 1950. It was the first time the West Indies defeated England in England in a Test series.What made their story even more remarkable was their lack of experience. Before the England tour, both Ramadhin and Valentine had played only two first-class matches each — both trial games for selection.England had prepared for the famous Three Ws — Frank Worrell, Everton Weekes and Clyde Walcott — who formed the backbone of West Indies' batting. What England had not prepared for was a pair of spinners with completely different styles.Ramadhin was famous for bowling both off-breaks and leg-breaks with almost no visible change in his action. Valentine bowled left-arm orthodox spin.Test debut at Old TraffordRamadhin and Valentine made their Test debuts together in the first Test at Old Trafford, Manchester, on June 8, 1950.West Indies lost that match by 202 runs, even though the pitch offered plenty of help for spin bowlers. Together, Ramadhin and Valentine took 15 wickets in the match, but England's spin trio of Jim Laker, Eric Hollies and Bob Berry used the conditions better.The defeat, however, was only the beginning of a historic series.Lords of Lord'sThe second Test at Lord's became one of the most iconic matches in West Indies cricket history. West Indies scored 326 in the first innings, thanks largely to Allan Rae's century. Ramadhin and Valentine then bowled England out for just 151.West Indies declared their second innings at 425 for 6 and set England a target of 601 runs.At the start of the final day — a Thursday — there were very few spectators at Lord's. Most of them were West Indians, and there were fewer than 100 in the crowd.England resumed at 281 for 4, chasing what was almost an impossible target.By lunch they had lost five more wickets. Shortly after 2.18 pm, Johnny Wardle was trapped lbw by Frank Worrell, and West Indies completed a 326-run victory, their first Test win over England in England. Ramadhin was the star of the match.He finished with figures of 5 for 66 in the first innings and 6 for 86 in the second. Valentine supported him with figures of 4 for 48 and 3 for 79.West Indies went on to win the remaining two Tests as well — by 10 wickets at Nottingham and by an innings and 56 runs at The Oval — to seal the series 3-1.Those two little pals of mine ...The victory at Lord's was iconic. But more iconic were the celebrations that followed.A small group of West Indian supporters ran onto the field carrying "guitar-like instruments", according to The Times. They danced, sang calypsos and created music using dustbin lids and even a carving knife scraped across a cheese grater.Among those supporters were Lord Kitchener and Lord Beginner, who had arrived in Britain aboard the Empire Windrush in 1948 as part of the first major wave of Caribbean immigrants.Lord Kitchener had been singing calypsos throughout the Test match. After the victory, he came up with lines that celebrated the heroes of the day:Walcott, Weekes and Worrell held up their nameWith wonder shots throughout the gameBut England was beaten clean out of timeWith the spin bowling of Ramadhin and Valentine.Those lines eventually became part of Cricket, Lovely Cricket, one of the most famous songs associated with West Indies cricket.There has been some confusion over who actually wrote the song. It was recorded and released by Lord Beginner, but there's some strong evidence to suggest that it was created jointly by Lord Beginner and Lord Kitchener.Former Southwark mayor Sam King, who was present at Lord's that day, recalled the moment in a 1998 interview with The Guardian."I was about going home, about 20 voices said, Sam, you can't go home, man. Kitchener going to make a song.' I said, What?' They said, Just come.' We sat down on the grass and Kitchener says, Cricket, lovely cricket,' and someone said, Put Ramadhin in, man.' And he put Ramadhin in, and he went over it, and in 30 minutes he wrote the song, Cricket, lovely cricket, at Lord's, where I saw it. Yardley won the toss, but Goddard won the Test, with those little pals of mine, Ramadhin and Valentine.' I was there. That was history."Whether it was written by one person or together, Cricket, Lovely Cricket became part of West Indies cricket folklore. The first stanza of calypso reads:Cricket lovely Cricket,At Lord's where I saw it;Cricket lovely Cricket,At Lord's where I saw it;Yardley tried his bestBut Goddard won the test.They gave the crowd plenty fun;Second Test and West Indies won. With those two little pals of mine, Ramadhin and Valentine.More than a one-series wonderRamadhin remained one of West Indies' mainstay through the 1950s. He was the leading wicket-taker in the 1953-54 home series against England, taking 23 wickets at an average of 24. Two years later, in New Zealand, he picked up 20 wickets at an average of 15.When West Indies returned to England in 1957, Ramadhin was still their biggest bowling weapon.In the first Test at Edgbaston, he produced the best innings figures of his Test career, 7 for 49. During one spell after lunch, he took 6 wickets for just 9 runs in eight overs.However, England responded tactically in the second innings.Peter May and Colin Cowdrey repeatedly stretched forward, using their pads to smother Ramadhin's spin because they believed lbw decisions would not be given.With two West Indies bowlers injured, captain John Goddard kept Ramadhin bowling almost continuously. Ramadhin bowled 98 overs in that innings, which remains a Test cricket record. Despite many appeals, the umpires didn't give any lbw in that innings.Ramadhin later became eligible to play county cricket after settling in England, and joined Lancashire in 1964.He also played Minor Counties cricket for Lincolnshire into his early forties and continued playing league cricket until he was nearly 50.After representing Lancashire and spending years in the Lancashire leagues as a professional, he settled permanently in north-west England following his retirement.He died on February 26, 2022, at the age of 92. A star of his time, Ramadhin, the first Indian to play for West Indies, claimed 158 wickets from 43 Tests during a 10-year international career.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'Age is just a number': Ishan Kishan confident of 'hungry' Mohammed Shami making India comeback
articles.summary: Cricket News: At 36, Mohammed Shami may be closer to the twilight of his career than its peak, but his desire to return to India colours remains as strong as ever. .
articles.body: At 36, Mohammed Shami may be closer to the twilight of his career than its peak, but his desire to return to India colours remains as strong as ever. That is the belief of East Zone captain Ishan Kishan, who has seen first-hand the veteran pacer’s determination during their run to the Duleep Trophy final.Shami, who has 903 wickets from 100 first-class matches, produced a match-winning spell in the semifinal against Central Zone in Bengaluru. For Kishan, however, it is not just Shami's performances that stand out, it is the hunger behind them.“I think he is just one of the best. He has been a legend of this game. He has been doing so well since he started playing for Bengal. He has been picking wickets, giving all his energy and he has done so well for the Indian cricket team also,” Kishan said at the pre-match press conference.While Shami is nearing the latter stages of his career, Kishan believes age should not be a barrier if the pacer continues to maintain his work ethic and hunger.“I feel age is just a number. If he is working hard it doesn't matter. I see that hunger in Shami bhai because who better than me to judge about hunger right now,” Kishan said, referring to his own period away from the Indian team.“Looking at his efforts as a captain, I felt very nice, because Shami bhai came in, asking me for those extra overs to get the wickets. This is something which always gives confidence to skippers. When you have bowlers who are willing to get you wickets, it's always good to have him in the team,” Kishan said.Shami even chipped in with the bat, striking two boundaries, prompting Kishan to jokingly label him an all-rounder.“He also finished with two boundaries, so he is an all-rounder I feel nowadays. So I am very happy to have him in my team,” he added.East Zone eye first Duleep Trophy title in 13 yearsEast Zone will take on South Zone in the Duleep Trophy final from Sunday, with a chance to lift the prestigious trophy for the first time since the 2012-13 season. East Zone defeated Central Zone in the semifinal to reach the final after 13 years. Their last title came in 2012-13, when they beat Central Zone to win their second Duleep Trophy.South Zone, meanwhile, are among the most successful teams in the competition, having won the title 12 times, with their most recent triumph coming in 2023. The final at Chepauk will also bring several India internationals and current white-ball stars together before the focus shifts to international cricket.Mohammed Siraj and Devdutt Padikkal have joined South Zone after featuring in India's recent 1-0 Test series victory over Sri Lanka, although KL Rahul is not expected to play the final.T20I specialists Tilak Varma, Ishan Kishan and Vaibhav Sooryavanshi have also been cleared by the BCCI to feature despite India's upcoming T20I series against Afghanistan, beginning September 13. articles.title: Eight runs needed, two wickets left: Auqib Nabi hits six before getting out next ball as Surrey pull off one-wicket win in County thriller
articles.summary: Cricket News: With two wickets left and six runs needed to win, Surrey looked close to victory against Yorkshire in their County Championship Division One match at .
articles.body: With two wickets left and six runs needed to win, Surrey looked close to victory against Yorkshire in their County Championship Division One match at The Kia Oval on Friday. India’s Auqib Nabi, making his County Championship debut, hit Ben Coad for a six over deep mid-wicket.The Surrey dressing room would have felt that the match was almost won. However, Nabi was caught at mid-on off the very next ball while attempting another boundary. That left Surrey needing two runs with their last wicket pair of Dan Worrall and Josh Blake at the crease.The two failed to score from the next 10 balls, including a maiden over from George Hill. Hill beat Blake’s outside edge five times during the over and finished with 4-52 from 23 overs. But Coad’s next delivery to Worrall brought the match to an end, as the No. 11 sliced the ball over square cover for the winning boundary.Surrey won by one wicket, narrowly denying Yorkshire the chance to defend their target of 185.Josh Blake and Matt Fisher played key roles in Surrey’s chase. Blake remained unbeaten on 43 from 183 balls, while Fisher scored 33 to complete a match in which he made an impact with both bat and ball against his native and former county.The pair came together when Surrey were 115-7 in pursuit of 185 and added 55 runs for the eighth wicket across 23 overs. Fisher was eventually dismissed after edging a drive from Hill to third slip.That brought Nabi to the crease and he immediately swung Coad for six. But with Surrey needing only two more runs, Nabi attempted another big shot and was caught at mid-on from the next delivery.Worrall and Blake then had to survive 10 balls without scoring before Worrall found the winning boundary off Coad.Fisher had revealed on the opening evening that he had started to fear relegation. A defeat would have left Surrey in a difficult position with three matches still to play. Instead, the victory lifted them above Yorkshire and moved them into mid-table.Brief score:Yorkshire 185 & 82: Luxton 29; Fisher 6-25Surrey 83 & 187-9: Blake 43*; Hill 4-52Surrey beat Yorkshire by 1 wicketGet the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: ‘Always in chaos, standing on one toe’: Matthew Hayden’s blunt verdict on Pakistan cricket amid latest turmoil
articles.summary: Cricket News: NEW DELHI: Pakistan cricket has once again found itself engulfed in turmoil, and former Australia opener Matthew Hayden believes the underlying proble.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Pakistan cricket has once again found itself engulfed in turmoil, and former Australia opener Matthew Hayden believes the underlying problem has remained unchanged for years.Hayden, who has previously worked with Pakistan as batting coach and team mentor, said the constant instability surrounding the setup makes it extremely difficult for players to perform consistently. His comments came after the Pakistan Cricket Board made sweeping changes following the team’s second successive defeat to England in the ongoing Test series.“I really enjoy and enjoyed my time working with Pakistan. Nothing’s changed, though. You know, that is always the trouble. That’s not an environment, you know; a pressure cooker is an environment for the middle, not for all the other peripheral things that happen outside. And it’s just too difficult an environment to be consistent because this is the formula,” Hayden said on the Wisden Cricket podcast.Pakistan lost the opening Test by an innings and 103 runs before suffering a 194-run defeat at Lord’s. England consequently took an unassailable 2-0 lead in the three-match series, prompting the PCB to overhaul the touring setup.‘They’re always standing on one toe’Hayden, who was Pakistan’s batting coach during their run to the semi-finals of the 2021 T20 World Cup and later served as a mentor during their 2022 campaign, believes the country possesses enough natural talent to compete with the best.“Pakistan are always dark horses, because their natural talent is phenomenal. I mean, anyone who can see athletic ability can see that Pakistan has an abundance of it. The trouble is, it never gets focussed because it’s never allowed to get focussed. It’s always in chaos. They’re always standing on one toe, let alone two feet. So there’s no grounding,” Hayden said.He added that bringing stability to the environment was one of the things he enjoyed most during his stint with Pakistan.“And that’s, you know, something that I did enjoy doing in the short time that I was with Pakistan. It’s just getting things back on an even keel and not so frantic. So it’s very difficult for them,” he added.The latest upheaval saw seven players sent home, including Mohammad Rizwan, Imam-ul-Haq, Salman Ali Agha, Ali Usman, Khurram Shahzad, Aamir Jamal and Muhammad Awais Zafar. Jamal and Zafar had not featured in either of the first two Tests.‘If Pakistan allows Pakistan to play freely’Hayden believes Pakistan’s enormous cricketing base should make it a global powerhouse, but said the country itself is preventing that potential from being fully realised.“Pakistan is that like the West Indies, who I specially mentioned, I would especially mention Pakistan as well, because you’ve got 350 million people in one country that adore cricket and yet every opportunity, cricket doesn’t allow cricket to get played,” he said.“And that old saying, it’s just not cricket that is so important for this conversation with Pakistan. Because if you allow Pakistan and Pakistan allows Pakistan to just play freely and with trust, then they’ll take on anyone as simple as that because purely their athletic ability like the West Indies is supreme,” Hayden added.PCB chief Naqvi defends the shake-upPCB chairman Mohsin Naqvi, meanwhile, has rejected suggestions that Pakistan cricket is finished, pointing to improvements in the white-ball formats and arguing that even leading teams suffer surprise defeats.“Let me ask you one thing: South Africa lost to Namibia, and India lost to Ireland. Has cricket ended there as well?” Naqvi said.He also defended the board’s changes, saying: “If someone is not clicking or not performing, then what can we do? Every match and every series is important for us.”But as Pakistan prepares for the third Test, Hayden’s assessment points to a problem deeper than results — the continuing inability to create the stability and trust he believes its immense talent needs.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: ‘Tough, but no excuses’: Ishan Kishan, Tilak Varma on going from Duleep Trophy final to Afghanistan T20Is
articles.summary: Cricket News: NEW DELHI: The switch from five-day red-ball cricket to the shortest format in a matter of days will be “slightly challenging”, Ishan Kishan and Tilak.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The switch from five-day red-ball cricket to the shortest format in a matter of days will be “slightly challenging”, Ishan Kishan and Tilak Varma admitted, but the India T20I stars are refusing to make the hectic schedule an excuse.Kishan and Tilak are set to lead East Zone and South Zone respectively in the Duleep Trophy final, which begins in Chennai on Sunday and runs until September 10. Just three days later, India begin their three-match T20I series against Afghanistan in New Delhi, leaving the players with only a couple of days to recover, travel and prepare for a completely different format.Kishan, who is also part of India’s T20I squad, acknowledged the difficulty of switching between formats and roles.“It is just about knowing what format you are playing. I know it gets difficult when you are playing Test match and suddenly you have to go and start hitting from ball one (in white ball format) and then suddenly you have to go back to your domestic team and you have to play a whole different role,” Kishan said in the pre-match press conference.Tilak, South Zone captain and India’s T20I vice-captain, echoed his teammate’s assessment.“Yes, it will be slightly challenging…playing five days here (Duleep Trophy) and again joining the (India) team. From here we are going to Delhi, so, there will be like a two day break. We can practise there. It will be slightly challenging,” he said.‘As professionals, it is our job to adapt’The key, according to both players, is adaptability. Having spent years moving between formats and playing back-to-back domestic and international matches, they believe they can make the mental and physical adjustment.“We have played enough domestic games, we have played in every condition, so we can adjust. We know how to change our mindsets and maintain our body with good fluids and everything.“We have played before in domestic as well as international back-to-back games, so we are quite used to it,” Kishan said.The East Zone captain also made it clear that players cannot complain about a schedule they already know they have to navigate.“I feel as professionals it is our job to adapt. We cannot come up with excuses after knowing this is your routine for the next few days. So, it is better to not be in a situation where we have to make excuses,” he added.“But at the same time be aware and be just mindful of what is going to happen and I will be playing T20I after this. So, my job will be different. But still I feel we are getting two days of practice before the first game against Afghanistan. So, it will be more than enough I feel.”Tilak had earlier made it clear that he wanted to play the Duleep Trophy final despite his India commitment, pointing to the two-day gap before the Afghanistan series. His participation was subsequently expected to go ahead, alongside Kishan and Vaibhav Sooryavanshi.Padikkal adds firepower to South ZoneSouth Zone will also be strengthened by the arrival of Devdutt Padikkal, who comes into the final after a spectacular Test series in Sri Lanka. He scored 328 runs in three innings, including two centuries, and was named Player of the Series.Tilak believes Padikkal’s form can make a significant difference to South’s batting line-up.“Yeah, it will be a big boost for us. The kind of form he (Padikkal) is in, it will be really helpful for us and he can share his experience with the players. We have got quite a few young guys on our side and it will be really helpful,” he said.The South skipper also confirmed Padikkal’s batting position.“Padikkal will be batting at number 3 and his coming into the side will strengthen our batting line-up, especially with the kind of form we have seen from Padikkal in the last 2 or 3 games. He has done really well. It will be a big boost for us,” he added.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi has already conquered IPL records and international cricket — now he faces another big test: his first five-day game
articles.summary: Cricket News: NEW DELHI: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi has barely had time to absorb one milestone before another arrives.At 15, the teenage sensation has already played on .
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi has barely had time to absorb one milestone before another arrives.At 15, the teenage sensation has already played on the biggest domestic stage, broken records in the IPL, made his international debut, starred at the Under-19 World Cup and established himself across T20, List A and first-class cricket. On Sunday, he will add another landmark to an extraordinary early career — playing his first five-day first-class match.Sooryavanshi will take the field for East Zone against South Zone in the Duleep Trophy final at the MA Chidambaram Stadium in Chennai, with the 15-year-old named vice-captain under Ishan Kishan.It is another challenge in a career that has been defined by the teenager repeatedly stepping into unfamiliar territory and finding a way to make an impact.For all his first-class experience, Sooryavanshi has so far played only four-day matches, whether for Bihar in the Ranji Trophy, India Under-19 or East Zone. The Duleep Trophy final will therefore represent his first experience of a five-day representative first-class fixture.And East Zone will expect him to play a significant role at the top of the order.Another format, another test for SooryavanshiThe youngster's ability to adapt has already been tested repeatedly this year.His first-class numbers remain modest compared to the astonishing figures he has produced in white-ball cricket — 347 runs from 10 matches, including two half-centuries. But his Duleep Trophy semifinal performance against Central Zone offered an encouraging glimpse of what he can produce in a longer format.Sooryavanshi smashed 92 off 81 balls in the first innings before contributing a crucial 40 in the chase as East Zone defeated Central Zone by four wickets to reach their first Duleep Trophy final since 2012-13.His 92 also made him the youngest player to score a half-century in Duleep Trophy history, at 15 years and 157 days, breaking a record that had stood for 57 years.Ishan Kishan, who will lead East Zone in the final, believes the teenager is already mature enough to handle the demands of another new challenge.“I feel Vaibhav is very smart for a 15-year-old boy. He knows what he is doing, he has been in this situation and I have heard him speaking to other players as well. So, there is no doubt if he has played 4 day or 3 day cricket earlier and this is a 5-day game, I think you just need to get runs out of him and that is what he is willing to do,” Kishan said in the pre-match press briefing on Saturday.Kishan was also impressed by the youngster's contribution in the semifinal.“I think he is doing a great job until now. He played a very crucial role in the previous match where the wicket was not that good but he played those extra shots which helped us get that opening partnership.”“It was very important while we were chasing. So he is doing everything right for now and if there is anything, I think we are there to always help him,” he added.From 14-year-old IPL centurion to India's youngest internationalThe scale of Sooryavanshi's rise becomes clearer when his journey over the past two seasons is considered.At 13, he became the youngest player to earn an IPL contract when Rajasthan Royals bought him for Rs 1.1 crore ahead of IPL 2025. A year later, at 14, he became the youngest centurion in men's T20 cricket when he smashed 101 off 38 balls against Gujarat Titans. He finished that season with 252 runs from seven matches at a strike rate of 206.55.Then came IPL 2026, when the teenager took his game to another level.Sooryavanshi scored 776 runs in 16 matches at a staggering strike rate of 237.30, with a century and five fifties. His 72 sixes broke the record for most sixes in a single IPL season, while he collected the Orange Cap and MVP award.He subsequently became India's youngest men's international debutant and made an immediate impact in the T20I series against Zimbabwe, scoring 151 runs in three matches and winning the Player of the Series award. His six T20I appearances have already yielded 193 runs at a strike rate of 189.21.His List A numbers are equally striking: 564 runs in 13 matches, including a 190, at an average of 43.38 and a strike rate of 176.80.At the Under-19 World Cup, meanwhile, he amassed 439 runs and was named Player of the Tournament.Now comes the five-day test: Duleep Trophy finalThe numbers suggest there is still plenty for Sooryavanshi to learn in the red-ball game. But that is precisely what makes Sunday's milestone significant. At an age when most cricketers are still finding their way through age-group cricket, he is already being asked to solve a new problem.Sooryavanshi has so far responded to almost every challenge with the same fearless approach that has made him one of the most talked-about young cricketers in the world.The Duleep Trophy final offers another test — not of how many records he can break, but of how he can adapt when the game demands patience, concentration and a willingness to bat for five days.At 15, there is no urgency for him to have all the answers.But another question is about to be asked of Vaibhav Sooryavanshi. And, judging by what he has done so far, another challenge is unlikely to intimidate him.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.summary: Cricket News: Former India batter Suresh Raina has backed Abhishek Sharma for a place in India’s Test setup while insisting that Rishabh Pant remains an X-factor in.
articles.body: Former India batter Suresh Raina has backed Abhishek Sharma for a place in India’s Test setup while insisting that Rishabh Pant remains an X-factor in white-ball cricket despite establishing himself as one of the country’s key red-ball players.Raina made the remarks while speaking on former India opener Aakash Chopra’s YouTube channel, where he also discussed the development of young players and the importance of encouraging them to consider Test cricket.Raina wants Abhishek to make the Test leapRaina believes Abhishek, who has emerged as one of India’s most explosive white-ball batters, has the ability to make the transition to the longest format.“I feel Abhishek Sharma should play Test cricket. Vaibhav is very young. Does he want to play? What do his coaches think? These are questions. I feel he should play. Are the IPL owners and associations also thinking of this and putting Test cricket in players' minds? Coaches also have a role here,” Raina said.Abhishek has already featured regularly for India in white-ball cricket and previously held the No.1 position in the ICC T20I batting rankings. While his red-ball numbers are not yet outstanding, he has shown enough promise to suggest that he could develop into a useful Test option.The left-hander has scored 1,071 runs in 24 first-class matches and 37 innings at an average of 30.60, with one century and five half-centuries. He has also contributed with the ball, taking 20 wickets in the format.Raina sees Pant as an X-factor in white-ball cricketRaina was equally effusive in his praise for Pant, who has become an established part of India’s Test setup but has been away from the limited-overs teams since 2024. Pant has amassed 3,725 runs in 52 Tests at an average of 43.82, including eight centuries and 21 half-centuries. His aggressive approach and ability to change the course of a match have made him one of India’s most influential Test batters.“He has worked hard. I am very happy. Everyone does well, but he is one of the best. He is my favourite player. He is scoring a lot in Tests. He has that X factor. I think he will mature in white-ball and IPL as well. He has done really well,” Raina said.Pant last played a T20I for India against Sri Lanka in Pallekele on July 28, 2024, while his most recent ODI appearance came against the same opposition in Colombo on August 7, 2024.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.body: Former West Indies captain Brian Lara has become the latest prominent cricket figure to voice support for imprisoned former Pakistan captain Imran Khan, calling for proper medical care and humane treatment for the 1992 World Cup-winning skipper.Lara took to Instagram to express his concern over Khan’s situation, saying he was struggling to understand how a sporting icon who once inspired an entire country could now find himself in circumstances where, in Lara’s view, he was not receiving the compassion and dignity he deserved."Imran Khan and I only crossed paths on the field a handful of times, but the respect I have for him was instant and lasting," Lara wrote in his Instagram post."I am struggling to understand how someone who was once a beacon of hope, pride and inspiration for his country, at the height of his sporting career, could now find himself in a situation where he is not being cared for and treated with the compassion and dignity he deserves."I stand with my fellow former captains in asking that he receive proper, independent medical care and the dignity every human being deserves. This isn't politics. It's basic humanity for a legend of our game," he added.Lara joins growing chorus of cricket greatsLara’s intervention comes amid growing concern among former and current international cricketers over Khan’s health and treatment in custody.A group of former international captains, led by former Australia skipper Greg Chappell, has repeatedly called for Khan to receive an independent medical assessment, continued family access and any treatment recommended by doctors. The latest appeal was signed by 21 former captains, including Sunil Gavaskar, Kapil Dev, Allan Border, Michael Atherton, Steve Waugh, Adam Gilchrist and Nasser Hussain.The signatories described themselves as former colleagues and rivals whose bond was forged on the cricket field and urged authorities to ensure that a court-directed medical process was properly completed.Their concerns have centred particularly on reports of significant vision problems affecting Khan’s right eye. articles.title: ‘Remarkable achievement’: Sourav Ganguly’s special message for Mohammed Shami ahead of 100th first-class game
articles.summary: Cricket News: NEW DELHI: Mohammed Shami is set to enter an elite club on Sunday when he makes his 100th first-class appearance in the Duleep Trophy final, and forme.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Mohammed Shami is set to enter an elite club on Sunday when he makes his 100th first-class appearance in the Duleep Trophy final, and former India captain Sourav Ganguly believes the milestone is a fitting reward for the veteran pacer’s remarkable longevity and contribution to Indian cricket.Shami will turn out for East Zone against South Zone at the MA Chidambaram Stadium in Chennai, with the occasion marking another significant chapter in a first-class career that has already produced 382 wickets from 99 matches. His best innings figures are 8/90.Ganguly, who played alongside Shami during the early stages of the pacer’s career, congratulated him on the landmark and highlighted the difficulty of sustaining a career as a fast bowler in the subcontinent."Dear Shami, congratulations on achieving this amazing feat - 100 first-class matches. As a fast bowler in the subcontinent, it's a remarkable achievement. I've seen you grow; I've played with you. It was the early stages of your career and the end of my international career. I always knew there was talent, but I'm extremely happy that you've used that talent to go this distance," Ganguly said in a video posted by CAB on Facebook.Ganguly also backed Shami to cap the milestone occasion with a Duleep Trophy title."And I enjoy the games. You're playing the Duleep Trophy final - it will be an icing on the cake if you win it. Your performances over the years have been fantastic, especially in Test cricket. You know, when fast bowlers shy away from playing Test cricket, you have a day-in, day-out run-in for India. Heartiest congratulations once again from my side and everyone at the Cricket Association of Bengal and the state of West Bengal. You know, it's a fabulous achievement. Enjoy the game and hope to see you soon," he added.Shami’s milestone comes amid India comeback bidThe landmark comes at a particularly interesting stage of Shami’s career. The 36-year-old remains outside India’s current setup but has continued to play domestic cricket as he looks to maintain his fitness and put himself in contention for another international recall. He last played for India in the Champions Trophy final in March 2025.Shami has made a strong impact in the Duleep Trophy. After going wicketless in East Zone’s opening match, he bounced back against defending champions Central Zone in the semi-final, taking five wickets across two innings as East secured a four-wicket victory and reached the final.‘Age is just a number’, says KishanEast Zone captain Ishan Kishan has been equally impressed by Shami’s determination and believes age should not stand in the way of the veteran’s ambitions.“I think he is just one of the best. He has been a legend of this game. He has been doing so well since he started playing for Bengal. He has been picking wickets, giving all his energy and he has done so well for the Indian cricket team also,” Kishan said at the pre-match press conference.“I feel age is just a number. If he is working hard it doesn't matter. I see that hunger in Shami bhai because who better than me to judge about hunger right now,” Kishan said, referring to his own period away from the Indian team.That hunger was visible during the semi-final, when Shami asked for additional overs in his pursuit of wickets.“Looking at his efforts as a captain, I felt very nice, because Shami bhai came in, asking me for those extra overs to get the wickets. This is something which always gives confidence to skippers. When you have bowlers who are willing to get you wickets, it's always good to have him in the team,” Kishan said.Shami even contributed with the bat, hitting two boundaries and prompting a light-hearted verdict from his captain.“He also finished with two boundaries, so he is an all-rounder I feel nowadays. So I am very happy to have him in my team,” he added.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.
