articles.title: India’s spin chokehold leaves Pakistan in tatters: 55 all out is their lowest-ever T20I total
articles.summary: Cricket News: NEW DELHI: Pakistan endured a dramatic batting collapse against India in their Women’s Asia Cup 2026 clash in Dubai on Saturday, crashing to their low.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Pakistan endured a dramatic batting collapse against India in their Women’s Asia Cup 2026 clash in Dubai on Saturday, crashing to their lowest-ever total in T20I cricket after being bowled out for just 55.After opting to bat first, Pakistan appeared to have an opportunity to put scoreboard pressure on India. Instead, their innings unravelled spectacularly as India’s bowlers turned the screw, with Pakistan losing six wickets for just eight runs after initially reaching 27 without loss.The 55 all out is now Pakistan’s lowest total in Women’s T20Is, surpassing their previous low of 56 against New Zealand in Dubai in 2024. It also becomes the fifth-lowest total conceded by India in a Women’s T20I.Only Pakistan’s two openers managed to cross double figures, with Muneeba Ali scoring 13 off 15 balls and Shawaal Zulfiqar making 14 from 14.Charani, Rawat trigger spectacular collapseThe slide began after Muneeba survived a couple of early scares before Shafali Verma eventually cleaned her up. Sree Charani then struck twice in the final over of the powerplay, turning Pakistan’s promising start into a full-blown collapse.Pakistan went from 27/0 to 35/6, with India’s spinners repeatedly breaching a batting line-up that struggled to cope with the pressure.Charani finished with outstanding figures of 3/7, while Prema Rawat also claimed three wickets for just nine runs. Deepti Sharma chipped in with 2/5 and Shafali Verma took one wicket.The Indian attack's ruthlessness was reflected in Pakistan's inability to build even a single substantial partnership after the opening stand. With wickets tumbling at regular intervals, the innings was wrapped up for 55 in 18.1 overs.Charani credited a simple approach for her success."Just (trying) to bowl to my strength, and coaches are telling all bowlers, spinners especially, to bowl to strength and give more revs on the ball. [What deliveries are you working on?] Trying to get more consistency on my arm ball and be more accurate on the yorkers," she said at the break.The performance underlined why India had entered the contest with such confidence in their bowling attack. India had already secured a place in the semi-finals after winning their opening two matches against Thailand and Hong Kong, while Pakistan came into the game having beaten Thailand.Pakistan’s unwanted record in 200th T20IThe collapse came on a significant occasion for Pakistan, who were playing their 200th T20I. Instead of celebrating the landmark with a competitive total, they ended the innings with a record they would rather forget.Pakistan’s previous lowest all-out total in the format was 56 against New Zealand in Dubai in 2024. Their other lowest totals included 60 against England in Taunton in 2009, 63 against India in Guangzhou in 2012 and 65 against the West Indies in St Andrew’s in 2011.For India, meanwhile, the 55 all out added another dominant chapter to their recent record against Pakistan. India had won nine of their previous 10 T20I meetings, with their only defeat in that stretch coming in the 2022 Asia Cup.The contest also marked Harmanpreet Kaur’s record 150th match as a T20I captain, making her the first cricketer, male or female, to reach the landmark.Lowest all-out totals for PAK-W in T20Is55 vs IND-W, Dubai, 202656 vs NZ-W, Dubai, 202460 vs ENG-W, Taunton, 200963 vs IND-W, Guangzhou, 201265 vs WI-W, St Andrew's, 201172 vs SL-W, Colombo (NCC), 2018Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.body: India produced a dominant all-round performance to thrash Pakistan by seven wickets in their Group A clash of the Women’s Asia Cup 2026 at the Dubai International Cricket Stadium on Saturday.After Pakistan opted to bat first, India’s spinners ran riot, bowling them out for just 55 in 18.1 overs, their lowest-ever total in T20Is. Despite those breakthroughs, the target was far too small to give Pakistan any genuine hope.Captain Harmanpreet Kaur held the chase together and finished unbeaten on 18 off 18 balls. She completed the victory in style, hitting a six as India reached 57/3 in 8.4 overs. articles.title: Irfan Pathan brings back viral 'Sunday' jibe as India beat Pakistan by 7 wickets in Women's Asia Cup 2026: Reason behind the famous banter revealed
articles.summary: After India Women beat their subcontinent rival Pakistan in a dominant seven-wicket victory, former India bowler Irfan Pathan brought his Sunday jibe back.
articles.body:
Irfan Pathan revived his viral "Sunday" jibe after India beat Pakistan by seven wickets.

The tradition dates back to Virat Kohli's iconic knock at the 2022 T20 World Cup.

India extended their winning run against Pakistan to nine matches across women's T20Is.

India W's seven-wicket victory leads to the return of Irfan Pathan Sunday Jibe

India's seven-wicket demolition of Pakistan in the Women's Asia Cup was still settling in when the most reliable post-match commentator in India-Pakistan cricket history hit send. Irfan Pathan took to X within minutes of the result, and the message needed only four words.

"Aaj Sunday hai kya?" the former India all-rounder posted , translating to "Is it Sunday today?" The match was played on a Friday, which is precisely what made it land.

For anyone who has followed the India-Pakistan rivalry on social media over the past four years, no further explanation was needed. For those who have not, the backstory is worth telling.

How Irfan Pathan's "Sunday" jibe became a tradition after Virat Kohli's iconic knock

The origin traces back to October 23, 2022, at the Melbourne Cricket Ground. India and Pakistan met in the T20 World Cup on a Sunday, and Virat Kohli produced one of the greatest T20I innings ever played, hauling India from 31 for 4 to a four-wicket victory with an unbeaten 82 off 53 balls.

As the cricket world processed what it had witnessed, Pathan posted a simple message to X that would define his social media presence for the next four years. "Padosiyon Sunday kaisa raha?" (Neighbours, how was your Sunday?) he wrote.

The tweet went viral instantly, and Pathan recognised he had struck gold. From that point forward, every India victory over Pakistan, regardless of the day of the week, the format or the gender of the teams involved, has been followed by a variation of the same theme.

Every time Irfan Pathan has used the "Sunday" jibe

The list has grown considerably since Melbourne. After India beat Pakistan in the 2025 Asia Cup final in Dubai on a Sunday, Pathan posted "Padosiyo, Sunday kaisa raha?" accompanied by a dance video set to Afghan Jalebi.

When India's men thrashed Pakistan by 61 runs at the 2026 T20 World Cup in Colombo, another Sunday fixture, he followed up with "Kaisa raha Sunday?" and a second clip addressing the "padosiyo" directly.

It extended beyond the men's game too. After India's women crushed Pakistan by 64 runs at the 2026 Women's T20 World Cup in Birmingham, Pathan posted simply "BEST SUNDAY", without even mentioning Pakistan by name.

When India won the World Cricket League in 2024, fans did not wait for Pathan to act, instead flooding his mentions with "Sunday wala tweet kardo" (post the Sunday tweet) before he had even opened the app.

Friday's post was the cleverest variation yet, because it acknowledged the tradition had outgrown any connection to the actual day of the week. By asking whether it was Sunday rather than declaring it, Pathan turned the absence of a Sunday into the joke itself.

Why Pathan's running gag has outlasted every other cricket meme

Most cricket memes have the lifespan of a T20 innings. Pathan's has survived four years and counting, largely because India has kept providing the results that feed it.

The women's side have now won nine of their last 10 T20Is against Pakistan, and India's combined men's and women's record in ICC and ACC events against their neighbours since Melbourne reads 11 wins from 12 completed matches.

As long as that run continues, so will the tweet. The only thing that could retire it is a Pakistan victory, and on current evidence, that looks some distance away.

articles.body: Pakistan's women's team slumped to their lowest-ever T20I total as India cruised to a seven-wicket win in their 2026 Women's Asia Cup Group A clash at the Dubai International Cricket Stadium on Saturday night.Opting to bat first, Pakistan made a reasonable start, reaching 27 without loss in the fifth over through openers Muneeba Ali (13, 15b, 1x4) and Shawaal Zulfiqar (14, 14b, 3x4), both of whom benefited from dropped chances.However, India's spinners took control soon after, triggering a dramatic collapse. articles.body: Chennai: Veteran India speedster Mohammed Shami maybe out of India reckoning for now, but he still refuses to give up. When East Zone play South Zone in the Duleep final at the MA Chidambaram Stadium here on Sunday, the 36-year-old will be appearing in his 100th First-Class match, with a prolific record of 382 wickets so far.East Zone skipper Ishan Kishan was effusive in his praise of the senior bowler on the eve of the title clash, stressing that age remains irrelevant when backed by exceptional work ethic and fierce determination."For Shami, age is just a number. If he is working hard, it doesn't matter. Having someone like him in our team gives us immense confidence. His approach towards the game, his intensity, and his energy this season have been very different from how I've seen him in the past," Kishan said after a practice session.Comparing this version of Shami to his sensational 24-wicket run at the 2023 ODI World Cup, Kishan stressed on the pacer's sheer appetite for a national comeback."It is 2026 now, three years since that World Cup. It is hard when you are not regularly playing for the Indian team to still summon that same motivation for domestic games...Who better than me can judge hunger right now? I see that hunger and drive in him, he wants to make that comeback and be part of the Indian squad again. You can see it in the way he helps me lead, constantly coming up with strategic options. You can instantly tell when a player is desperate to win you the match," the skipper added.Kishan also hailed Shami's tireless attitude during East Zone's semifinal victory over Central Zone, where the veteran ran in and picked five wickets in the game."He is a legend of the game. Looking at his effort in the semifinal, as a captain, it felt incredible when Shami came up and asked for extra overs to break partnerships. That willingness gives a skipper immense confidence. Plus, he finished with two boundaries in the last game, so he's practically an allrounder nowadays," Kishan quipped.South Zone captain Tilak Varma acknowledged the massive challenge awaiting his batting unit against Shami's probing spells with the red ball, but they are confident to face him."It will be great competition. articles.title: Match fixing concerns? PCB takes Pakistan players’ phones into custody before final England Test
articles.summary: Cricket News: Pakistan’s troubled England tour has taken another unexpected turn, with the Pakistan Cricket Board reportedly taking mobile phones belonging to membe.
articles.body: Pakistan’s troubled England tour has taken another unexpected turn, with the Pakistan Cricket Board reportedly taking mobile phones belonging to members of the national team into its custody ahead of the third and final Test at Edgbaston.According to Pakistani 365 News, the players’ devices have been handed over to the PCB and will remain with the board until the conclusion of the final Test. The report did not reveal the identities of the players whose phones were taken, while the PCB has not publicly stated why the devices were placed in its custody.The development has raised questions about the extent of the authorities’ powers over players’ personal devices, particularly regarding when phones can be seized, retained or accessed and what safeguards apply to private communications.What do ICC rules say about players’ mobile phones?Mobile phones are already subject to strict restrictions in international cricket, particularly inside areas designated as restricted during matches.Under the ICC’s Player and Match Officials Area regulations, players and support staff are not permitted to possess or use mobile phones or other communication devices inside restricted areas, including dressing rooms, during an international match.Players are expected to place their devices in secure storage before entering such areas. The primary purpose of these regulations is to protect the integrity of international matches and prevent unauthorised communication.However, those match-day restrictions are separate from a situation in which a player’s personal phone is retained for an extended period.The ICC Anti-Corruption Code gives authorised anti-corruption officials considerably broader powers when a formal integrity investigation is underway.Under the code, an authorised anti-corruption official can make a written demand requiring a participant to surrender a mobile device or allow investigators to copy or download information from it when there are reasonable grounds to believe the material could be relevant to an investigation.The information potentially covered by such a request is wide-ranging. It can include telephone and internet records, text messages, WhatsApp conversations, photographs, videos, audio files and other electronically stored documents.Participants can also be required to provide passwords or access codes needed by investigators to obtain the relevant material.A failure to comply with a legitimate demand during an anti-corruption investigation can itself result in disciplinary action.No confirmation of corruption investigationDespite the ICC’s provisions, the reported decision by the PCB to take possession of the players’ phones does not, by itself, establish that an anti-corruption investigation is taking place.There has been no confirmation that the PCB’s action in England is connected to an integrity investigation involving corruption, betting or match-fixing. No player has been publicly accused of an integrity offence either.There is also a distinction between the ICC’s jurisdiction and the authority of national cricket boards.For international cricket, the ICC’s Integrity Unit has primary authority under the global Anti-Corruption Code, while national boards generally have direct anti-corruption jurisdiction over domestic competitions.The PCB could also have separate powers arising from player contracts, team regulations or internal disciplinary procedures. However, the board has not publicly cited any such provision as the reason for the latest move.Another setback on a chaotic England tourThe phone controversy comes at a particularly difficult stage of Pakistan’s tour of England.After heavy defeats in the opening two Tests, the PCB overhauled the squad mid-series. Seven players were sent back to Pakistan, and the coaching staff was reshuffled ahead of the Edgbaston finale. Test coach Sarfaraz Ahmed has been replaced by Mike Hesson, who will oversee Pakistan in the third and final Test.The decision to place players’ mobile phones in PCB custody adds another unusual development to an already turbulent tour.For now, however, the precise reason behind the move remains unclear. Until the PCB provides an explanation, it cannot be established whether the phone custody is linked to an internal disciplinary matter, team regulations or any formal integrity-related process.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: ‘200, 300 mar de’: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi’s coach makes huge demand ahead of Duleep Trophy final
articles.summary: Cricket News: Kolkata: On Teacher’s Day, the eve of the Duleep Trophy final, Manish Ojha has one particular wish — that his most famous ward, Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, .
articles.body: Kolkata: On Teacher’s Day, the eve of the Duleep Trophy final, Manish Ojha has one particular wish — that his most famous ward, Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, produces a record-breaking knock when East Zone take on South Zone in the title clash starting Sunday.Vaibhav’s childhood coach, who watched East Zone’s semifinal in Bengaluru, is in Chennai for Sunday’s title clash against South Zone, hoping the 15-year-old can make the most of a venue where he has already left his mark. Vaibhav scored 104 for India A against Australia A in a Youth Test here on Oct 1, two years ago, and Ojha believes that familiarity could work in his favour as he bids to strengthen his red-ball credentials.However, Vaibhav will not be the only player from Bihar and Jharkhand under the spotlight. East’s campaign has been powered by a strong contingent from the two states, with captain Ishan Kishan, Vaibhav, Anukul Roy and Mukesh Kumar regulars in the side, while Virat Singh and Kumar Kushagra add further depth. They are complemented by Bengal’s Mohammed Shami and Abhimanyu Easwaran, giving East a blend of youth and proven red-ball experience.The stakes are higher with the national selection panel, led by chief selector Ajit Agarkar, expected to watch the final. For Ishan and Vaibhav, in particular, the match offers a chance to underline their red-ball worth in front of the selectors and strengthen their cases for India’s Test setup.“Vaibhav has his own method and his own way of making runs. Ultimately, what matters is the performance and whether you are making runs for your team. He does that. His style of making runs is different,” Ojha told STOI from Chennai on Saturday.The coach is also impressed by the maturity Vaibhav is beginning to show despite his age and aggressive approach.“He is not even 16 yet, so give him time. Slowly, as he keeps playing, you can see the maturity coming into his game. According to the situation of the match, he is starting to change his game little by little,” Ojha said.“By the time he is 24, I feel he will still have another eight to 12 years of cricket ahead of him. You will expect a lot from him then, and I believe he will stand up to those expectations.”East’s return to the final after 14 years carries historical significance. Their last Duleep Trophy triumph came in the 2012-13 season, when they defeated Central Zone in the final in Chennai. A return to the city gives the current side an opportunity to recreate that piece of history.Former India and Jharkhand cricketer Shahbaz Nadeem believes East’s balance makes them strong contenders against South Zone.“Look at Shami, look at Ishan, look at Virat Singh and Anukul. There is a lot of experience as well as young blood. I think this mixture of youth and experience is a very good and, I would say, deadly combination,” Nadeem said.For Nadeem, reaching the final itself is a significant achievement for East after such a long wait.“It is always a premier tournament in India. If you are playing the final of such a tournament and representing a zonal team, there is nothing bigger than getting an opportunity to perform there. East Zone are reaching the final after many years, so I think it is very important for the boys,” he said.Nadeem also expects Anukul to play an important role in Chennai after a productive run in domestic cricket and with India A recently.“I think he will be quite useful on the Chennai wicket because he also bowls. His batting is also a plus point and his fielding is another plus point. This will be an important match for him to prove himself and give the selectors a statement that ‘I also belong at that level’,” he said.Meanwhile, for Ojha, Saturday’s Teacher’s Day has a special resonance. He is in Chennai watching a pupil he helped shape take another step towards the highest level.His wish for Sunday is simple. “Main to chahta hun wo 200 mar de, 300 mar de, sab record tod de (I wish him to score 200, 300 (in the game) and smash all the records,” Ojha says in jest and hopes Vaibhav turns his familiarity with the Chennai pitch into a big red-ball statement — and perhaps another record to remember.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: India thrash Pakistan for 55, Wahab Riaz still calls them ‘best side’ in Asia Cup
articles.summary: Cricket News: Pakistan’s Women’s Asia Cup campaign appears to be operating in a rather interesting parallel universe.On the field, Pakistan were blown away by India.
articles.body: Pakistan’s Women’s Asia Cup campaign appears to be operating in a rather interesting parallel universe.On the field, Pakistan were blown away by India, bundled out for just 55 in 18.1 overs and then beaten by seven wickets in a little over eight overs. Off the field, however, Pakistan women’s team mentor Wahab Riaz remains convinced that his side are the best team in the tournament and have what it takes to win the trophy.India made the Pakistan batting line-up look completely helpless at the Dubai International Stadium on Saturday night, with young spinners Shree Charani and Prema Rawat doing most of the damage. Yet, despite one of Pakistan’s most emphatic defeats in the format, Riaz insisted that the conditions could still work in his team’s favour.“I believe that all the players in our team are very skilful and they just need to trust themselves. Our next match is against Hong Kong. We will go back and discuss what we did wrong against India. We will try not to commit the same mistakes. I still believe Pakistan is the best side in this Asia Cup to lift the trophy because the conditions really suit us,” Riaz told reporters after the match against India.If India’s seven-wicket victory was the reality check, Riaz’s assessment suggested Pakistan were still firmly committed to looking at the brighter version of events.Pakistan’s 55-run reality checkPakistan entered the contest needing a strong performance against the tournament favourites. Instead, their batting collapsed spectacularly.Shafali Verma began the demolition by bowling Muneeba Ali for 13, before Charani struck twice in the sixth over. Gull Feroza departed for a duck, while Shawaal Zulfiqar was dismissed for 14, leaving Pakistan at 29 for 3.From there, the innings went rapidly downhill.Pakistan slipped to 32 for 4 in the eighth over and were reduced to 45 for 7 in the 13th. Charani finished with 3/7, while Rawat claimed 3/9. Deepti Sharma also played her part with 2/5 as Pakistan were eventually dismissed for 55 in 18.1 overs.It was Pakistan’s lowest-ever T20I total.Their previous lowest score had been 63, made in 19.1 overs against India in Guangzhou during the group stage of the 2012 Women’s Twenty20 Asia Cup.India, meanwhile, needed only 8.4 overs to chase down the target, losing three wickets along the way. Harmanpreet Kaur remained unbeaten on 18 to complete a victory that never looked remotely in danger.Wahab disagrees with Sana MirRiaz was also asked about criticism from former Pakistan captain Sana Mir, who had questioned the management’s decision to make wholesale changes to the squad for the tournament.Seven players were left out, but Riaz defended the selection calls and argued that the changes were made with the future in mind.“Sana Mir has her own opinion. I have nothing to do with that opinion. We have made changes with the future in mind. The players who were playing before, they have played a lot of World Cups and Asia Cups but we weren't getting the results. So it was time to go with new faces and bring new girls into the mix to build the team for the upcoming tournaments,” Riaz said.He was equally clear that the players left out had not done enough to retain their places.“It is not about who we left behind. We have to look at the reality. The girls who were left out weren't performing at all. I think we did the right move by bringing new girls into the mix,” he added.The timing of Riaz’s assessment could hardly have been more striking.Pakistan had just suffered their heaviest batting collapse in T20I history against India, while India extended their perfect run in the tournament to three matches and secured their place in the semi-finals with six points.Pakistan, on two points, now need to beat Hong Kong in their final group match to keep their qualification hopes alive.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.summary: Cricket News: Indian left-arm spinner Sai Kishore starred with the ball as Gloucestershire defeated Derbyshire by 213 runs in the County Championship Division Two m.
articles.body: Indian left-arm spinner Sai Kishore starred with the ball as Gloucestershire defeated Derbyshire by 213 runs in the County Championship Division Two match at the Seat Unique Stadium in Bristol.Sai Kishore returned figures of 5-20 from 18 overs as Derbyshire, chasing 319, were bowled out for 105 inside 39 overs during the final session of the match.Ed Middleton supported him with 2-17, while Ollie Price took 3-59, with Gloucestershire's spin attack claiming all 10 wickets in Derbyshire's second innings.The victory completed a turnaround for Gloucestershire, who had been reduced to 37-5 on the opening day of the match.Earlier, Gloucestershire declared their second innings at 359-5. Miles Hammond scored 118, while James Bracey remained unbeaten on 104. The pair added 165 runs for the fourth wicket.Bracey became the first Gloucestershire batter to score two centuries in the same first-class match since Alex Gidman achieved the feat at Archdeacon Meadow, Gloucester, in 2007.The win earned bottom-placed Gloucestershire 19 points and ended a run of six consecutive defeats. Their only two wins this season have both come against Derbyshire, who left Bristol with four points.Derbyshire needed early wickets when play resumed with Gloucestershire at 149-3, but they missed key chances in the field.Shoaib Bashir dropped Bracey off his own bowling when the batter was on five, while Matt Montgomery failed to hold a return catch to dismiss Hammond on 77.The missed opportunities proved costly as Hammond and Bracey took control. Bracey reached his second half-century of the match from 75 balls, while Hammond completed his third first-class century of the season and the eighth of his career from 182 deliveries.Derbyshire took the new ball and brought back seamers Ben Aitchison and Brett Randell, but Gloucestershire reached 268-3 by lunch.After helping Gloucestershire into a strong position, Hammond was dismissed when Montgomery caught him at mid-wicket off Martin Andersson. His innings combined defence and attack.Bracey then completed his fifth century of the season from 143 balls, hitting seven fours and two sixes before Gloucestershire declared at 359-5. He also became the first Gloucestershire wicketkeeper to score two centuries in a match since Harry Smith in 1919.Set 319 to win, Derbyshire's approach was focused on survival rather than chasing the target. Gloucestershire opened the bowling with spin from both ends and packed the field around the bat.Sai Kishore made an immediate impact after tea. He trapped Harry Came lbw and then bowled Matt Montgomery with the very next delivery.Soon after, Wayne Madsen was caught at second slip off Sai Kishore as Derbyshire slipped to 32-3.Mohammed Bin Naeem was then trapped lbw by Ollie Price after a delivery stayed low.Derbyshire's collapse continued as Sai Kishore bowled Aneurin Donald and Brooke Guest within three deliveries, completing his five-wicket haul inside eight overs.Middleton replaced Price from the Ashley Down Road End and had Ben Aitchison caught by Ollie Price at second slip with Derbyshire at 76-7.Martin Andersson, who top-scored with 35, was then caught at first slip after edging Middleton while trying to defend.Price wrapped up the innings by trapping Jack Morley lbw and then dismissing Brett Randell in front. He finished with match figures of 9-104 as Gloucestershire completed a 213-run win in front of home supporters.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.body: Former India bowling coach Bharat Arun has questioned the way Mohammed Shami has been treated by the current selection committee led by Ajit Agarkar, insisting that the veteran pacer still has plenty to offer despite being out of the national setup.Shami has not played for India since the Champions Trophy campaign in March 2025, when India went on to win the tournament. Since then, the 36-year-old has remained outside the national team despite putting together a series of strong performances in domestic cricket.His continued absence has fuelled speculation that Shami's international career could be nearing its end. However, Arun believes India should not have shut the door on one of their most experienced fast bowlers.Bharat Arun unhappy with Shami's treatmentShami's omission has been particularly noticeable when Jasprit Bumrah has been unavailable, with the Indian management opting to invest in younger pace options rather than recall the experienced Bengal seamer.There was also a public exchange between Shami and Agarkar last year. After the selectors left Shami out of the Test squad for the series against the West Indies, Agarkar raised questions about the pacer's fitness.Shami responded by making it clear that he would not have been playing Ranji Trophy cricket for Bengal had he not been fit.With Shami continuing to perform strongly on the domestic circuit, Arun believes age should not automatically count against him.“They shouldn’t have closed the door on Shami. There is still plenty of cricket left in him. When someone is performing, age shouldn’t be a factor. You see his durability. It is an outstanding number for the kind of talent he possesses. It is actually befitting for Shami. 100 first-class matches with what he loves most, the red ball,” Arun told the Indian Express.Shami is currently representing East Zone in the Duleep Trophy final against South Zone in Chennai, giving him another opportunity to make his case with the red ball.Ishan Kishan also sees hunger in ShamiEast Zone captain Ishan Kishan has also noticed a different level of intensity from Shami during the current domestic season.Speaking ahead of the Duleep Trophy final, Kishan said the veteran pacer has shown a strong desire to make an India comeback and praised the effort he has been putting into his domestic cricket.“As a captain, looking at the effort, I felt very nice, because Shami bhai coming in, asking me for those extra overs to get the wickets, it always gives confidence,” Ishan said.Kishan added that Shami's attitude has stood out to him, particularly given that he is no longer a regular member of the Indian team.“Looking at Shami bhai this season, I feel he has been very different. I’ve seen him in the past, but his approach towards the game, his intensity, his energy has been very different. When you are not regularly playing for the Indian team and to again have that same kind of motivation for your domestic games, it is tough but I feel I see that hunger in him. I think he has that hunger and that motivation right now like he wants to do that comeback, he wants to be part of Indian squad again and which you can see in him," he added.Shami reaches 100 first-class matchesThe Duleep Trophy final has also provided Shami with another significant milestone.The East Zone pacer has featured in his 100th first-class match against South Zone in Chennai, adding another landmark to an accomplished career.Shami also played an important role in East Zone's semi-final victory over defending champions Central Zone, claiming three wickets in the second innings.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Fatima Sana’s fiery Shafali Verma send-off draws savage response: ‘Your entire team just scored 55’
articles.summary: Cricket News: Pakistan captain Fatima Sana found herself at the centre of attention during her side’s Women’s Asia Cup clash against India at the Dubai Internationa.
articles.body: Pakistan captain Fatima Sana found herself at the centre of attention during her side’s Women’s Asia Cup clash against India at the Dubai International Stadium on Saturday.Sana did manage to make an impact with the ball, claiming three wickets as Pakistan were bowled out for just 55. But it was her animated celebration after dismissing India opener Shafali Verma that became one of the talking points of the contest.The incident occurred on the third ball of the second over of India's chase. Sana delivered a good-length ball that bounced slightly more than Shafali expected.The young opener attempted to work it towards the leg side but only managed to produce a leading edge. The ball went back towards Sana, who held on comfortably to complete the catch.Sana immediately turned towards Shafali and gestured towards the pavilion, giving the Indian batter a fiery send-off.Shafali, however, showed no reaction to the celebration and simply walked back towards the dressing room. She had made 12 off six deliveries, hitting one four and one boundary before her dismissal.The send-off also drew a sharp observation from commentator Vivek Razdan, who pointed out the contrasting fortunes of the two teams.“Okay, you are showing her the way out. Your entire team just scored 55 runs, and now you're sending Shafali Verma back,” Razdan said on air. Pakistan batting collapseSana's dismissal of Shafali was her third wicket of the innings, as the Pakistan captain tried to lead from the front after her own team's disastrous batting display.Pakistan had initially appeared comfortable after being asked to bat first. Muneeba Ali and Shawaal Zulfiqar put on a confident start, taking the score to 27 without loss in a little over four overs.That progress quickly disappeared once India turned to spin.Youngsters Shree Charani and Prema Rawat dismantled the Pakistan middle order with disciplined spells, while Deepti Sharma also joined the attack as Pakistan lost six wickets for only nine runs.Charani, a 22-year-old left-arm orthodox spinner, finished with outstanding figures of 3/7 from four overs. Rawat, the 24-year-old leg-spinner, claimed 3/9 in her four overs.Shafali also contributed with the ball, picking up one wicket for 10 runs from three overs, while Deepti returned 2/5 from 3.1 overs.Pakistan eventually folded for 55 in 18.1 overs, their lowest-ever total in T20I cricket.India's bowlers were relentless throughout the innings, delivering an astonishing 78 dot balls.India complete another one-sided win over PakistanThere was little drama once India began their chase.Shafali was dismissed for 12, while Smriti Mandhana made nine and Pratika Rawal scored four, with Sana accounting for all three wickets.But Pakistan had no scoreboard pressure to work with after their own collapse, and Harmanpreet Kaur and Deepti Sharma comfortably guided India home.Harmanpreet remained unbeaten on 18, while Deepti finished not out on 12 as India reached the target in only 8.4 overs to complete a seven-wicket victory.The result also gave Harmanpreet another landmark. She became the first captain in international cricket, men or women, to lead India in 150 T20Is.She fittingly sealed the victory with a six down the ground.India had entered the contest looking for some valuable match practice before the semi-finals, but Pakistan's batting collapse turned the fixture into another one-sided affair.The result extended India's dominance in the T20 Asia Cup, with the Indian women now having seven wins over Pakistan's one in the tournament's history.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Pakistan were bowled out for their lowest-ever T20I total of 55 before India chased down the target with 68 balls to spare and registered a seven-wicket win on Saturday.India had already secured a semifinal place from Group A before the match. They finished top of the group with six points after winning all three games.Charani, who dismissed Shawaal Zulfiqar, Gull Feroza and Ayesha Zafar, said the team’s spin bowlers discuss their plans before every match and then try to follow them on the field."In the meeting, we three sit together... Prema, me, Deepti di and Radha (Yadav) di and we discuss what to do (in the match). So, we just try to implement that here (on the field) whatever Deepti and Radha di say," said Charani.Pakistan had raced to 27 without loss, but Charani struck twice in the sixth over to leave them at 29/3. They could not recover after that and were eventually bowled out for 55.The 22-year-old is now one wicket away from completing 50 T20I wickets. She said her approach was to keep things simple and concentrate on getting the basics right."It's just about myself. Like I just want to focus on my things... I want to do my things correct," she said.After looking at the pitch and expecting it to help the spinners, Charani said she focused on bowling at the stumps and allowing the pitch to do the rest."I just tried to bowl on the stumps. articles.title: Eight runs from one ball: Andrew Symonds produced one of Test cricket’s strangest feats, but it still wasn’t the highest ever
articles.summary: Cricket News: Andrew Symonds once produced one of the rarest scoring feats in Test cricket, collecting eight runs from a single delivery during Australia's Test aga.
articles.body: Andrew Symonds once produced one of the rarest scoring feats in Test cricket, collecting eight runs from a single delivery during Australia's Test against New Zealand at the Gabba in Brisbane in 2008-09.The bizarre sequence involved an all-run four followed by four overthrows, with New Zealand fast bowler Iain O'Brien at the centre of the drama. There was an added twist to the incident, as O'Brien had seen Symonds dropped off the previous delivery before eventually dismissing him just two balls later.How Symonds ran eight off one ballAustralia were 124 for four in the 46th over after Ricky Ponting had decided to bat in Brisbane.O'Brien opened the over with a bouncer, which Symonds ducked under. The bowler went short again with his next delivery, and this time Symonds pulled the ball towards mid-wicket.However, Aaron Redmond put down the chance.O'Brien responded as fast bowlers often do after a missed opportunity, sending down another short delivery. This time, the ball was outside off-stump and Symonds attacked it ferociously with a pull.The enormous Gabba outfield slowed the ball down, but Symonds and Michael Clarke had already completed three runs by the time Redmond got to it.The pair then decided to push for another run, hoping to take advantage of the throw.That decision produced chaos.New Zealand wicketkeeper Brendon McCullum moved across to collect the return. He gathered the ball, turned and threw it towards the stumps, only to discover that Symonds had already made his ground.There was another problem for New Zealand. Nobody was positioned behind the wicketkeeper to stop the throw.The ball therefore continued all the way to the boundary. Symonds had effectively turned a pull shot into an extraordinary eight-run haul.Umpire Rudi Koertzen then signalled the total by raising eight fingers, meaning eight runs were added to Australia's score and Symonds' tally.It was two more than the figure commonly described as the maximum possible from a single delivery and even one more than the total India received in a penalty-run incident against Bangladesh at Chattogram.Symonds was not the only batter to score eightSymonds' eight-run delivery was only the fourth known instance of eight runs being scored from a single ball in Test cricket at that point.The first recorded example came in Melbourne during the 1928-29 series, which was also the final Test of Don Bradman's first series.England's Patsy Hendren scored eight after completing four runs and then benefiting from four overthrows off Australian debutant Percy Hornibrook.Another unusual eight-run delivery occurred in Melbourne during the 1980-81 season.New Zealand's John Wright was the beneficiary on that occasion. He ran four before four overthrows followed after Rod Marsh collected the fielder's return and threw the ball towards the stumps. The throw escaped and Wright picked up the additional runs off Lenny Pascoe's delivery.The other known instance before Symonds came in Port-of-Spain during the 2004-05 season.Brian Lara glanced a delivery from South Africa's slow left-armer Nicky Boje for three. South African wicketkeeper Mark Boucher chased the ball and threw it back towards the field.However, Boucher's return struck a fielder's helmet that had been left on the ground.That resulted in five penalty runs being awarded, taking Lara's total from the delivery to eight.Under the rules at the time, those five runs would previously have been credited to Lara. Following a recent rule change, they were instead recorded as penalty extras.Lara, who was on his way to a huge score, would eventually be dismissed for 196.Nine runs from one ball is even rarerEight runs from one delivery are extraordinarily unusual, but first-class cricket has witnessed an even greater number.There have been 14 recorded instances of a batter running nine runs from a single ball in first-class cricket. Remarkably, none of those instances came after 1949.Only one of those 14 was achieved without the help of overthrows. Frederick Ponsonby of the MCC managed it against Cambridge University at Parker's Piece in Cambridge in 1842.Even that record was surpassed in unusual circumstances by Samuel Wood of Derbyshire against Cuthbert Burnup of the MCC at Lord's in 1900.That match was played during an experimental period involving the 'revised net system'. Boundaries were removed at some first-class matches and replaced by high nets surrounding the playing area.With no boundaries to end a run, batters had to keep running for every scoring opportunity.It was a completely different approach to scoring, but it also produced one of cricket's most extraordinary statistical records.Symonds' eight at the Gabba, meanwhile, remains one of the game's most memorable examples of how a single delivery can turn into complete chaos, combining a powerful shot, aggressive running and a disastrous throw into one remarkable sequence.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'They play second-team players': Former India cricketer warns BCCI over SENA warm-up matches
articles.summary: Cricket News: Former India cricketer Aakash Chopra has welcomed the BCCI's move to make warm-up matches compulsory before tours of SENA countries, but said the bigg.
articles.body: Former India cricketer Aakash Chopra has welcomed the BCCI's move to make warm-up matches compulsory before tours of SENA countries, but said the bigger challenge will be ensuring those matches are played against quality opposition.The BCCI recently held a review meeting at its Mumbai headquarters ahead of India's T20I series against Afghanistan. The meeting was attended by board secretary Devajit Saikia, head coach Gautam Gambhir and Centre of Excellence head VVS Laxman. India captains Shubman Gill and Shreyas Iyer were also part of the discussions.In a video on his YouTube channel, Chopra said the idea of mandatory warm-up games is a positive step, but only if the matches provide proper preparation."If you are going to SENA countries, there will be mandatory warm-up games. There was an era when the England tour used to last the entire summer. It was a four-month tour where you played matches against county teams," Chopra said.He recalled that those county matches used to be competitive and helped Indian teams prepare for the Test series."Theoretically, it isn’t wrong, but I don’t know how to maintain the quality of those games. I don’t have the answer for that at the moment because, of the time I am talking about, the teams used to be good and they used to almost beat us," Chopra said.Chopra pointed out that things have changed over the years, with county sides often fielding second-string teams in tour matches.“Now they play their second-team players, saying the match has no significance. So that one thing is still missing. The quality will have to be maintained a little," Chopra added.The former opener said mandatory warm-up games are still a move in the right direction because they offer better preparation than shadow A-team tours before a major series.His comments came days after BCCI secretary Devajit Saikia said the board wants to improve the team's preparation before tours of South Africa, Australia, England and New Zealand.After the review meeting in Mumbai, Saikia said the BCCI plans to give players enough time for rest, acclimatisation and practice matches through future tour scheduling.“We have instructed our FTP persons who will be meeting very soon in various international forums that our FTP should be in such a way it should be scheduled that there is proper rest for the players as well as some kind of acclimatisation or some kind of friendly matches before any major series in SENA countries (South Africa, Australia, England and New Zealand),” Saikia said following the review meeting at the BCCI headquarters.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'Pakistan cricket in shambles, all-time low': Ex-cricketer tears into PCB amid England turmoil
articles.summary: Cricket News: NEW DELHI: Pakistan cricket is going through a major crisis. With the team already 2-0 down in the three-Test series against England, the Pakistan Cri.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Pakistan cricket is going through a major crisis. With the team already 2-0 down in the three-Test series against England, the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) has made a series of sudden changes that have raised more questions than answers. Former Pakistan wicketkeeper-batter Atiq-uz-Zaman has expressed his disappointment over the situation, saying the team is currently “in shambles” and at an “all-time low”.Pakistan suffered a heavy 194-run defeat at Lord’s in the second Test. Soon after, the PCB made a major overhaul ahead of the third and final Test at Edgbaston, starting September 9.Seven players, head coach Sarfaraz Ahmed and bowling coach Umar Gul were sent home. White-ball coaches Mike Hesson and Ashley Noffke were asked to take charge of the red-ball team, while former captain Misbah-ul-Haq resigned from the selection panel and also stepped away from his batting consultant role at the National Cricket Academy in Lahore.The changes have added to the uncertainty around a Pakistan team already struggling across formats.‘Pakistan cricket is in shambles’Atiq-uz-Zaman questioned the decision to make so many changes in the middle of a Test series, especially the decision to send some players home."I don't understand why Khurram Shehzad was dropped or why the spinner (Ali Usman) was sent home after taking the most wickets in the Leeds Test. All of a sudden, now T20 bowlers are brought into the Test squad. Why? Because Mike Hesson has his personal favourites, and he brought those players into Test cricket."I don't understand what's going on. Pakistan cricket is in shambles at the moment. It really hurts me because, even though I live in England, I am Pakistani at heart. I played for my country and I want them to improve and perform well in different conditions. Pakistan cricket is currently at an all-time low," Atiq-uz-Zaman told IANS.‘There is no justification for it’He also questioned the decision to remove Sarfaraz and Gul from their coaching roles midway through the series.“There is no justification for it. The same people who selected them are the ones turning around and deselecting them. That means either you made a mistake in the first place, or you are making a mistake right now."Look, Sarfaraz Ahmed and Umar Gul are greats of Pakistan cricket. They’ve won World Cups for Pakistan. Sarfaraz won a World Cup at the U19 level and then won the Champions Trophy as national captain. He deserves respect. Now, I personally didn't agree with him becoming the Pakistan Test team head coach because he lacked prior coaching experience and qualifications."I didn't support that appointment. But once you make him the coach, you have to back him. Give him a fair chance before you disrespect him and send him home in the middle of a Test series. It is unacceptable. I feel very sorry for Sarfaraz and Umar Gul because I don't think they did anything wrong. If the players on the field can't perform, or if you haven't selected a team capable of performing, what is a coach supposed to do? Let's see what Mike Hesson does now," he added.Atiq questions Imam’s decision not to batAtiq-uz-Zaman also criticised Pakistan opener Imam-ul-Haq, who did not bat in the Lord’s Test after suffering a Grade 1 tear in his left calf.Imam did come out for some batting practice despite the injury, but his decision not to bat in the Test drew criticism.Atiq said he would have expected the opener to come out and bat even if he was not fully fit.“Look, I won't speculate on the exact severity of his injury, but in our culture, we are raised to be tough. If you have a Grade 1, 2, or even Grade 3 muscle strain, you still step out there and bat for your team. Even if you get out on the first ball, it doesn't matter - the public sees that you showed heart, and they respect you for it.“Instead, he made himself look bad by not batting in either innings, and then walking out in front of the media in shorts with bandages on his leg and heavily limping - even if you can't run, you can still hit a ball. Look at Glenn Maxwell scoring a double hundred with severe hamstring cramps, or Chris Woakes coming out to bat with a fractured hand. Look at Saleem Malik playing against West Indies fast bowlers with a broken arm.“Imam-ul-Haq should have walked out to bat. Even if he got out immediately, nobody would have questioned his commitment because he was genuinely injured. But limping around in front of the media after taking criticism the day before just looks like a performance.“It leaves a bad impression, and I have no sympathy for that behaviour. If you don't have the heart or bravery for international cricket, you shouldn't be playing Test matches. Test cricket isn't just a test of your skills - it's a test of your character,” he elaborated.‘Enjoy your cricket and believe in your skills’Despite his criticism, Atiq-uz-Zaman backed the players to respond in the final Test at Edgbaston.He said Pakistan players have grown up in a difficult system and must focus on their cricket despite the uncertainty around them.“To be honest, in Pakistan, players are used to this environment from domestic, U16, and U19 cricket. We are raised in a tough system where you rarely get total freedom or backing, and you always feel like you are playing under threat just to survive. My message to them is: enjoy your cricket, believe in your skill set, do what you can with bat and ball, and leave the rest to God.”‘Talent in Pakistan is undeniably there’Atiq, who works as a scout for England women's, Lions and Young Lions and coaches the Germany men's team, also called for major changes at the PCB level.He believes Pakistan has enough talent but needs better leadership, planning and support to develop that talent."Hopefully, the PCB chairman changes his approach and brings in someone with genuine expertise and leadership experience to drive real structural change. If you surround the team with quality, professional individuals, they will instill high standards. The talent in Pakistan is undeniably there, but without the right resources and supportive structure, these players cannot reach the next level."Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'Win against India damaged us a lot': Mohammad Yousuf explains Pakistan cricket's decline
articles.summary: Cricket News: NEW DELHI: Former Pakistan star cricketer Mohammad Yousuf has said the country's current cricket crisis began after their famous 10-wicket win over In.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Former Pakistan star cricketer Mohammad Yousuf has said the country's current cricket crisis began after their famous 10-wicket win over India at the 2021 T20 World Cup in Dubai.Pakistan had never beaten India in a World Cup before that match. Babar Azam scored an unbeaten 68, while Mohammad Rizwan made 79 not out as Pakistan chased down 152 without losing a wicket. The win was celebrated as a historic moment for Pakistan cricket.However, Yousuf believes the victory also changed the mindset of the players and played a role in the team's decline in the years that followed.'That match... damaged us a lot'Yousuf said the players became too confident after beating India and failed to understand what they needed to do next.“That match which we won against India in 2021, that damaged us a lot. Because after that victory, players started to think that they had achieved something big. They couldn’t understand what they had to do next. When you are performing well, you should stay humble. If you behave with your collar raised, and get disrespectful, problems will arrive. And a lot of them have arrived in Pakistan cricket,” said Yousuf in a conversation on Samaa TV.Yousuf believes the problem was not only about Pakistan's results. He feels the team's attitude also changed after the famous win.Players wanted to become captainYousuf also blamed the fight for captaincy for some of Pakistan's problems.He said players became more interested in becoming the team's captain instead of taking responsibility for their performances.“Everyone in the team was trying to become the captain of the Pakistan team. The consequences are still hurting Pakistan cricket. Look at all the cricket Pakistan has played in the last four-five years, from ODI World Cups, T20 World Cups to Asia Cups and Champions Trophy. There has been terrible cricket. The PCB has been supporting you throughout. So many coaches have come and gone, so many things have changed just to try and help the Pakistan team. But no player has stood up and taken responsibility. Eventually, PCB had to take a step that it did. I back what PCB did,” added Yousuf.Pakistan in trouble in EnglandYousuf's comments have come at a difficult time for Pakistan cricket. The team suffered heavy defeats in the first two Tests against England. Pakistan lost the Headingley Test by an innings and 103 runs before suffering a 194-run defeat at Lord's. The Pakistan Cricket Board then made major changes in the middle of the England tour.Seven players - Mohammad Rizwan, Imam-ul-Haq, Salman Ali Agha, Ali Usman, Khurram Shahzad, Aamir Jamal and Muhammad Awais Jafar - were sent back to Pakistan with one Test still left in the series.The PCB also removed head coach Sarfaraz Ahmed and assistant coach Umar Gul. Seven replacements were called up, including five uncapped players.The decision to make major changes in the middle of a Test series attracted a lot of attention. However, Yousuf said he had no problem with the PCB's decision.When asked whether the board was right to take action with one Test still remaining, he said: “Yes, there is no issue with when PCB have taken action. The Pakistan team is ninth in the World Test Championship standings. They are ninth because there are only nine teams in the table. Pakistan ka naam kharab ho raha hai (Pakistan’s reputation is getting ruined). So when that’s happening, the board has to take some steps to improve.”Yousuf also suggested that something may have happened inside the dressing room that led to the seven players being sent home.'It's not just this one series'Yousuf said Pakistan's problems cannot be blamed only on the ongoing England series.He pointed to the team's poor performances in major tournaments over the last few years.“I don’t see an issue with the PCB reaction. Because the team has been playing terrible cricket. It’s not just this one series against England. We played in the T20 World Cup final in 2022 and played in an Asia Cup final as well, but since those finals, just look at the performances coming out of this Pakistan team,” Yousuf said.Pakistan have struggled across formats in recent years.
